News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

Sports.title: Newcastle now have ideal opportunity to sign 236-goal World Cup striker this summer
Sports.content:
Newcastle now have ideal opportunity to sign 236-goal World Cup striker this summer

Newcastle United could change their transfer plans after Eddie Howe's departure from the club

View 2 Images Newcastle United could change their transfer plans after Eddie Howe's exit (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)

Newcastle United and Eddie Howe parting ways could provide the perfect opportunity for Ivan Toney to return to St James’ Park. Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle is considered the favourite to replace Howe as Newcastle boss and the 38-year-old has coached Toney for the last two seasons.

‌



The former Brentford star completed a £40million move to the Saudi Pro League in 2024 and has been prolific for Jaissle’s side. Toney, who was included in England’s recent World Cup squad, has scored 72 goals in 93 games for Al-Ahli, helping the club secure back-to-back AFC Champions League triumphs.

‌



Newcastle's strikers struggled for goals last season after making two big-money signings to replace Alexander Isak, with Nick Woltemade fading after an impressive start and Yoane Wissa ending his debut campaign with a solitary league goal. William Osula offered hope as he ended the season with a flourish but the Magpies could potentially look to add more firepower.

‌



It is worth noting that a move for Toney would represent a departure from the club’s current transfer policy, with all four of their summer signings being younger than 21. While there is no suggestion that Newcastle are currently interested in Toney, the experienced striker could prove to be a shrewd addition as Newcastle look to revamp their squad.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Despite moving away from the Premier League, Toney has clearly not lost his goalscoring instincts after finishing last season with 42 goals. He has scored 236 club goals throughout his career, including his three-year spell in the top flight with Brentford, where he memorably hit the 20-goal mark in 2023.

‌



Eddie Howe gets England job verdict as Thomas Tuchel stance taken after Newcastle bombshell READ MORE :

If Jaissle takes Howe’s place in the Newcastle hotseat, the 38-year-old knows how to play to Toney’s strengths. The striker would add another dimension to Newcastle’s striking options and has already proven he can play alongside Wissa.

The pair featured in 71 matches together for Brentford, with Toney scoring 31 and Wissa finding the net on 16 occasions, respectively. Scoring a total 47 goals in 71 games is proof that Newcastle could revive a fruitful attack by bringing Toney back to the club.

The 30-year-old previously joined Newcastle as a teenager in 2015 after making his first team breakthrough at Northampton Town. He ultimately made just four appearances and experienced six loan spells before being sold to Peterborough United in 2018.

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has worked with Toney since 2024 (Image: Neville Hopwood/Getty Images)

Returning to the Magpies would signal a full-circle moment for Toney and allow him to finally make his mark at the club. However, it would be more than a sentimental move, with Toney helping to bring the best out of Newcastle’s misfiring attack.

When recently asked about his best position by former Bayern Munich star Thomas Muller, Woltemade said: "Preferably in a two-striker system or behind the striker. It's better for me to play with a lot of freedom and when I have someone around me."

‌



Adding Toney to the Newcastle squad would give the club four senior strikers and the option to create multiple combinations. While Woltemade and Wissa lacked cohesion last term, signing Toney would give the incoming Newcastle boss fresh possibilities.

It remains to be seen whether Jaissle will be appointed Newcastle manager and if the club choose to recruit a striker in the final few weeks of the window. However, with two years left on his Al-Ahli contract, Toney should not be overlooked by Premier League clubs searching for a centre-forward.

Sports.title: Franco Baresi: An all-time great who defined an iconic club and an entire nation
Sports.content:
Franco Baresi: An all-time great who defined an iconic club and an entire nation

Trubutes to the AC Milan and Italy defender have been pouring in after he died at the age of 66 and the game is united in acclaiming him as one of its best defenders

View 3 Images Franco Baresi will be remembered as one of football's greatest-ever defenders

There are good players, great players, players who define a club, players whose charisma has lit up the game. And then, there are players who, somehow, just come to symbolise how a nation plays its football, what its football stands for, what its football is based on.

‌



Johan Cruyff and Holland, Pele and Brazil, Franco Baresi and Italy. It is quite simple. When you think Baresi, you think vintage Italian football.

‌



You think extreme defensive know-how and brilliance. You think ruthless elegance. You think building from the back. You think style.

‌



Baresi, who has passed away at the age of 66, was not just a footballer - he was a way of playing football. He was someone who made the art of defence compelling.

Gianni Infantino facing imminent FIFA wipeout as UEFA could take nuclear option READ MORE :

Baresi was the totem of Italy’s golden footballing generation. He was the totem of the great AC Milan side - managed by Fabio Capello - that went on a 58-game unbeaten league run, earning them the nickname ‘Gli Invincibili’. No translation needed.

The backline of that team read: Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Costacurta, Franco Baresi, Mauro Tassotti. Alexa - define ruthless, define cool, define class.

‌



For those of us from a certain generation, watching those defenders operate was fascinating. Baresi was not a commanding figure but one who exuded such intelligent authority.

He could play as a sweeper, a more conventional centre-half, or even occasionally move into what we now recognise as a pivot in front of the defence. He is one of the greatest defenders in the history of the sport.

View 3 Images AC Milan retired Franco Baresi's shirt after his 20 seasons at the club (Image: AC Milan via Getty Images)

‌



The records show that he was part of the Italian squad that won the World Cup in 1982 but Baresi did not play in that tournament. Instead, of his 81 caps for the national team, his finest two hours came in a losing cause in the 1994 final in Pasadena.

He was 34 and had suffered a meniscus tear in the second game of the group stage against Norway. Yet just over three weeks later, he returned for the final against Brazil.

The game finished goalless after extra-time as Baresi, without injured team-mates Costacurta and Tassotti, put on a display that is widely acknowledged as one of the finest defensive masterclasses in World Cup history. Beset by cramp and fatigue after 120 minutes, Baresi was one of those who missed a penalty in the shootout and played only one more game for his country.

‌



He would carry on playing for his beloved AC Milan, the 1996-97 season being his 20th and last. His number six shirt was retired.

View 3 Images Fabio Capello and Franco Baresi took the great AC Milan side on a 58-game unbeaten league run (Image: Getty Images)

“The entire history of AC Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi,” the club said. “His example and integrity will be forever etched into the club’s DNA, just as his iconic number six shirt is.”

‌



Baresi won six Serie A titles, three European Cups, two Intercontinental Cups and three European Super Cups. He was runner-up to Milan team-mate Marco van Basten in the 1989 Ballon D’Or vote but individual accolades were a side-issue for Baresi.

It was all about Milan, all about Italy, all about defending. And that will be the special legacy of a truly great player.

Sports.content:
Sandro Tonali lifts like on talks held with Tottenham while at Newcastle

Sandro Tonali and Roberto De Zerbi have opened up on the secret talks they held before his move from Newcastle United to Tottenham.

Speaking to football.london, the Spurs boss said: "The story is very simple. I saw Sandro wanted to leave before the end of the season, before our Chelsea game, and we have one friend in common, the team manager of Brescia.

"I read a story which said 'Tonali is leaving Newcastle in the summer', and I messaged my friend to say 'hey, inform Sandro, if we stay up, I'll go to him'.

"After 10 minutes, my friend answered 'I said to Sandro and he's open'. Now we have to win one game to stay up! I watched Newcastle's game against West Ham, 90 minutes like this (indicates sweat pouring down his face), and Sandro played very well in the first half. I said [to myself] 'if I stay up, I come to you, I come to you, I come to you'.

"When we won the final match against Everton, the day after I sent a message to him - 'Sandro, I want to speak with you'. After 10 minutes, we spoke, and after two days I went back to Italy and we met in his home. I didn't want to invite him to mine, because I thought maybe he's not comfortable in my home. I preferred to keep him in the right condition to say 'yes, why not'."

Tonali then added: "Brescia is so small. I spent two weeks there, him as well, and I met him two or three times in the city, but not just him. I met my old team manager in Brescia. I met Roberto Baggio twice!

"I had spoken with [De Zerbi] when he was in Sassuolo, Marseille and Brighton. We spoke every time because we are Italian, from Brescia, and it’s a mini connection together.

"I spoke with another team, but when I spoke with Tottenham, it was totally different. They spoke with 100 per cent passion. Roberto and the director made the difference to the deal."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change

Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan is receiving more and more opposition against his plans to change the World Cup and other competitions for good

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino has been dealt another reality check amid his plans for the World Cup (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have announced their opposition to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell shares in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. After CONCACAF and UEFA, they have become the latest confederation to express their opposition to the plan, which is to create a commercial subsidiary called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' which would then look to sell 20-30 per-cent of its stocks to private investors.

‌



Forty-seven countries make up the AFC, which means up to 143 nations are already against Infantino's proposal, with 55 making up UEFA and a further 41 making up CONCACAF. With FIFA being formed of 211 member nations, Infantino's plan is in danger of fizzling out before it ever really got started.

‌



It's understood he needs over 50 per cent of member associations to support his plan for it to go ahead. The AFC's statement is the latest brutal reality check for the Swiss figurehead.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In a statement, following similar positions set out by UEFA and CONCACAF, they wrote: "The AFC stands in solidarity with UEFA and CONCACAF in expressing serious concerns over FIFA’s proposal to introduce private investment into FIFA's flagship competitions and the decision-making process around FFE. The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game. Football should never have been placed in such a position.

"Against this backdrop, and in light of the clear positions expressed by UEFA and CONCACAF, as well as the unprecedented divisions that have emerged across the football world, the AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward. The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world’s leading football nations. Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered.

‌



"While the immediate debate centres on FFE, the AFC considers this issue extends far beyond a single proposal. Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed. While the AFC notes FIFA’s latest clarification on the proposal, the central concerns surrounding governance, institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is bleeding support (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A proposal of such significance, with the potential to affect the commercial, sporting and strategic future of world football, must not emerge through processes that leave Confederations, Member Associations (MAs) and even FIFA’s own governing bodies, including the FIFA Council, feeling side-lined. The primary objective for world football must be to ensure that decisions of such magnitude are being developed through processes that are anchored on transparency and command the confidence of the football community.

‌



"This is not the first occasion where major stakeholders have been confronted with significant initiatives after the direction of travel appears to have already been determined. Such an approach undermines confidence in FIFA’s governance framework and diminishes the authority of its statutory bodies.

"No subsequent consultation process, however well intentioned, can replace early engagement with the appropriate FIFA bodies and the football family. The AFC believes this moment must become a catalyst for strengthening institutional reform.

View 3 Images Things look set to get worse for Gianni Infantino (Image: PA)

‌



"While every FIFA MA must have the opportunity to consider and determine proposals affecting the future of world football, meaningful democracy is not measured solely by the opportunity to vote. It begins with transparent governance, timely consultation, informed deliberation and genuine participation throughout the decision-making process.

"Accordingly, the AFC calls upon FIFA to undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework to ensure that proposals of global significance are developed through proper consultation, meaningful engagement and appropriate oversight by FIFA’s statutory bodies. The FIFA World Cup, and the game itself, belong to the entire global football family. Their future must always be shaped collectively, through institutions that reflect the voices of all Confederations and MAs."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino facing imminent FIFA wipeout as UEFA could take nuclear option
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino facing imminent FIFA wipeout as UEFA could take nuclear option

As Gianni Infantino's vision for the World Cup continues to invoke ire and fury across the football world, the FIFA president may be putting his position at risk

View 3 Images UEFA emphatically rejected FIFA's proposal (Image: Getty Images)

A vote of no confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino may only need the support of 20 per cent of member nations. Infantino, 56, has driven a wedge through football with his plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

‌



UEFA has already stated its 55 member nations will boycott all FIFA competitions until the plan is consigned to history, while CONCACAF, the federation for North America, Central America and the Caribbean nations, publicly stated it's against the proposal. It's understood Infantino only needs just over 50% of support from FIFA's member associations, but the rejection of the aforementioned federations means up to 96 are already against him.

‌



FIFA issued a new statement this morning insisting "nobody is selling football" but it has done little to quell the anger. While Infantino was expected to be re-elected until 2031 unopposed, there is a mechanism which could extract him out of his role.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

World Cup winner Franco Baresi dies aged 66 as tributes flood in for Italy and AC Milan icon READ MORE :

Article 25(4) of FIFA's statutes state only 20 per cent of member nations, or 43 countries, are required to launch a vote of no confidence. UEFA could look to convene an emergency FIFA Congress to launch this vote.

Moreover, it's also possible a new candidate to lead FIFA could be put forward. UEFA had been trying to persuade Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser al-Khelaifi to challenge Infantino, but it's understood the Qatari has no appetite to do so.

‌



While CONCACAF outlined its intention to oppose the plan, the Mexican Federation appeared to distance itself from their statement. They wrote: "The FMF will complete this process of study and analysis in order to take the decision that ⁠best serves the development of Mexican football."

View 3 Images Infantino's position could be coming under threat (Image: PA)

FIFA have also tried to reclaim the narrative about the competition by releasing another statement, claiming "incorrect media reports" has painted the vision in a bad light.

‌



They wrote: "We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

"We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation. Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.”

View 3 Images Infantino reportedly briefed the Trump administration on these plans (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



It added: "FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries.

"This does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself. Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's confirmed salary, FIFA president's wife and shocking World Cup plan
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's confirmed salary, FIFA president's wife and shocking World Cup plan

Gianni Infantino has been FIFA president since 2016 and has rocked the footballing world with his proposed plans for the World Cup

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino has been FIFA president since 2016 (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has sent shockwaves through the footballing world after plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup were revealed. The FIFA president has faced backlash after it emerged that the sport’s world governing body wanted to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) to run its events and would allow external investment.

‌



Infantino has given FIFA’s 211 member associations until September 19 to accept the proposal, promising each around £30million ($40m) for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, beginning with a payment of approximately £15m ($20m) in January 2027. However, European governing body UEFA has responded by announcing plans for its 55 member associations to boycott FIFA competitions while the proposal is under discussion.

‌



FIFA’s reported proposals suggest that the governing body would own the majority of FFE, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations’ stake totalling 20 per cent. Responding to the criticism on Wednesday, Infantino said: "FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer.

‌



"It's part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino's salary

Infantino has been FIFA president since succeeding Sepp Blatter in 2016 and was re-elected in 2019 and 2023. He had previously worked for UEFA, beginning in 2000.

‌



UEFA have one problem in toppling Gianni Infantino from power at FIFA over World Cup plan READ MORE :

FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup READ MORE :

According to FIFA, the 56-year-old’s base salary is around £2.39m (Fr.2.6m), with a variable salary of approximately £2m (Fr.2.2m). He is also permitted £22,1000 (Fr.24,000) in flat-rate allowances.

During his time in football governance, Infantino has expanded the men’s European Championships to 24 teams and helped create the UEFA Nations League. As FIFA president, he has expanded the World Cup to 48 teams, with the Women’s World Cup set to follow the same format in 2031, and overhauled the Club World Cup.

Wife Leena Al Ashqar

Infantino has been married to his wife Leena Al Ashqar since 2001. The couple reportedly met through Leena’s work for the Lebanese Football Federation and they have four children together.

‌



Infantino became a Lebanese citizen in February, the country his wife is from. The family have previously spent time in Doha, Qatar but Infantino officially moved his residency to Zug, Switzerland in June 2022.

View 3 Images Infantino and his wife Leena Al Ashqar have four children together (Image: Roberto SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

Shocking World Cup plan

Infantino’s plan to sell shares in FIFA’s competitions has been condemned by UEFA and CONCACAF, with the latter comprising of North and Central American nations, including the USA and Canada. On Thursday, a UEFA statement read : "UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions. UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one.

‌



“We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.”

CONCACAF echoed UEFA’s stance, with its respective statement reading: “During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned.

‌



View 3 Images Infantino has been criticised for his World Cup plans (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

“The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance. For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal.”

However, FIFA responded on Friday, following UEFA's and CONCACAF's rejection of the plans. A FIFA statement said: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday. We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

‌



⁠”Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.”

The statement continued: “FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself. Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino under threat as nations 'lose faith' in FIFA boss over World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino under threat as nations 'lose faith' in FIFA boss over World Cup plot

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is coming under mounting pressure as support for him continues to lessen following threats from UEFA, who insist they will boycott the next World Cup if he pushes forward with his proposal

View Image FIFA President Gianni Infantino is losing support across the globe - raising questions over his position

Gianni Infantino is losing support to remain as FIFA president after his World Cup plan went up in smoke with countries ready to boycott the tournament.

‌



The FIFA boss announced earlier this week a proposal to sell part of the tournament to private investors, but 90 of the 211 football associations are now against his plan.

‌



UEFA held an emergency meeting where they unanimously agreed to boycott the World Cup in 2030 - leaving the likes of England, France and champions Spain absent - if FIFA did go forward with their plan to create commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, with external investors able to buy stakes in it.

‌



Infantino now faces a battle to survive this latest controversy with the backlash against him growing rapidly.

FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino's plan for World Cup explained as FIFA put on notice over boycott READ MORE :

It is understood that the majority of the 41 CONCACAF members are losing confidence in Infantino and their leader, Victor Montagliani of Canada, is a potential successor if Infantino is forced out. Equally UEFA would like to see PSG's president Nasser Al-Khelaifi go for the role.

Infantino's predecessor Sepp Blatter quit amid scandal and a growing backlash in 2015, which saw Infantino become president in 2016, but this is the biggest challenge to his status.

‌



The FIFA boss has proved a hugely divisive figure following controversial decisions that included expanding the World Cup, which saw FIFA charge huge sums for tickets and ignore the game's rule to put on a final half-time show. Infantino has also created a new Club World Cup, effectively to rival the Champions League.

UEFA's statement and show of defiance has led to a backtrack from FIFA, who now have declared "no one is selling football" while attempting to blame 'incorrect media reports'.

‌



There has been fury, with UEFA and several of its members leading the way, that FIFA head Gianni Infantino has been secretly working on partly selling off the money-making parts of the governing body to external investors.

In a forceful Europe's governing bod said after meeting with all 55 member associations: "This model has no place in world football. Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

"As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."

Sports.title: Donald Trump on collision course as FIFA's worst-case scenario over World Cup plans unfolds
Sports.content:
Donald Trump on collision course as FIFA's worst-case scenario over World Cup plans unfolds

Gianni Infantino's FIFA World Cup plans have been rejected by CONCACAF, which includes the United States, and could see the FIFA president forced into an awkward conversation with Donald Trump

View Image Donald Trump has reportedly been briefed on FIFA's plans (Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

U.S. Soccer, as part of CONCACAF, has publicly opposed Gianni Infantino's World Cup proposals, despite reports that President Donald Trump's administration had been briefed on the plans.

‌



The football federation for North and Central America, alongside the Caribbean, openly voiced its opposition to Infantino's vision, which sought to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise to consolidate FIFA's commercial operations, spanning sponsorship, ticketing, licensing and broadcasting - alongside tournament delivery.

‌



The scheme then involved offloading a minority stake, believed to be somewhere between 20 and 30 per cent, to private investors, including figures with connections to Trump. Joshua Kushner, brother of the US president's son-in-law Jared, was amongst the backers behind the proposal.

‌



The Trump administration was also thought to have been consulted regarding the scheme, which has been publicly rebuffed by UEFA, who declared it will boycott all FIFA competitions until the proposal is abandoned. While CONCACAF held back from threatening competition withdrawals, it has made its lack of support for the plan abundantly clear.

FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup READ MORE :

Man Utd transfer talks confirmed as agent says deal is close READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Following their own statement's release, US Soccer's X account emphasised their public resistance to Infantino.

‌



It stated: "U.S. Soccer stands with Concacaf and its members," shortly after CONCACAF publicly declared they will not back Infantino's proposal.

Given that Trump's administration was consulted about the concept, the fact the US' equivalent to the Football Association has so openly rejected the scheme represents a setback to both Infantino and Trump and could force the pair into an uncomfortable discussion in the very near future.

Furthermore, the embattled FIFA president also indicated his proposal required backing from just over 50 per cent of FIFA's 211 member nations to proceed. With UEFA and CONCACAF already opposing it, he has already lost 96 nations (55 in UEFA and 41 in CONCACAF).

‌



In their statement, the federation representing North and South America wrote: "Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first. Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organisation founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football.

"History has shown FIFA and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values. With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its FIFA Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the FIFA President to establish 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' and sell interests in the FIFA World Cup to private investors.

‌



"During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned.

"The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance. For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal.

"Tasked their FIFA Council Members with engaging FIFA to determine how existing vast FIFA reserves could be used to increase FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region; and tasked their FIFA Council Members with instructing the FIFA President to ensure that any matter follows the proper governance processes via staff and FIFA Council, in accordance with the FIFA Statutes.

"Through these actions, Concacaf reaffirms that football's future-and its greatest asset-must remain in the hands of our football family."

Sports.title: Are Bournemouth set to strike defender gold again with Silva?
Sports.content:
There was a time when Antonio Silva's rise to the top appeared an inevitability. He was only 18 years old when he scored his first Champions League goal for Benfica in a 4-3 win over Juventus. He played at the 2022 World Cup for Portugal soon after that.

Since then, Silva has been linked with Europe's biggest clubs but it is Bournemouth who look set to sign him after agreeing a deal with Benfica. In truth, excluded from Portugal's squad this summer, his momentum has stalled. But, aged 22, there is time for this move to ignite his career.

Sure, there are grander destinations. But Bournemouth have emerged as one of the best recruiters of talent - proving themselves particularly adept at developing defenders. Silva is entitled to believe he can be the next to flourish for the Cherries.

Illia Zabarnyi and Dean Huijsen left for Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, respectively, just one year ago. Marcos Senesi has since moved to Tottenham. Silva is special enough to impress every bit as much as his predecessors on the south coast.

Speaking to Joao Nuno Fonseca, Silva's coach during his days with Benfica's development team, there is confidence that Bournemouth boss Marco Rose may have a gem in his hands. "Marco will not have any problems with him," Fonseca tells Sky Sports.

"Antonio is a very good person and the type of player that is easy to coach. He is very attentive. At Benfica, he listened to every detail that we gave him. He was very mature and that had a huge impact because it is difficult to reach the first team at Benfica."

Silva did that swiftly in part because of this mentality. "You give him feedback and he applies it directly in games. He understands everything." It made for a precocious talent in his teenage years, boasting an appreciation of time and space that belied his years.

"The key aspect of his game is his anticipation. Antonio reads the game really well. He is an anticipation-based defender rather than a reactive one. You see a lot of reactive centre-backs. He is not one of those. Antonio understands what will happen next."

Fonseca notes that the feet are good too. But it is the mind that saw Silva rise so quickly. "The technical skills are there, of course. But the key difference is understanding the game, in possession and out of possession. He knows what to do in those moments."

He praises the timing of his tackles. "He is one of the best in this technical aspect." And Silva's statistics show a defender who is aggressive in winning interceptions and aerial duels. Important qualities given that Bournemouth will expect him to be proactive.

In possession, Silva has the confidence to play forwards rather than simply recycling possession. "He is a modern ball-playing centre-back, very comfortable receiving the ball on either foot." There is variety to his use of the ball, chipped passes and more.

"One of the best things he has is the diagonal switches that he can do without looking," says Fonseca. "He is very, very talented at that." Expect that to be a significant feature at Bournemouth, who are looking to retain elements of Andoni Iraola's vertical approach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch some of Bournemouth's best team goals under Andoni Iraola

It is why Rose is regarded as the continuity candidate. Iraola is on record as an admirer of the former Borussia Dortmund coach who honed his ideas in the Red Bull school where looking forward and pressing high up the pitch are viewed as non-negotiables.

"I think it will work fantastically because of the way Antonio reads situations," says Fonseca. "Marco will demand anticipation, a defender who looks for forward passes that break the lines and find those spaces in behind. Antonio will adapt very quickly."

The Premier League will still be different. Even after four years at Benfica - perhaps especially after four years at Benfica - it will feel a step up. "This move is fantastic for him because he will evolve and mature much more as a player in the Premier League."

Did he stay in Portugal too long? "He needed to move earlier, in my opinion," concedes Fonseca. "He stayed longer than expected. The decision that he made not to leave Benfica last year did not help him because he needed exposure to new experiences."

He explains: "We used to say at Benfica that while life starts at Benfica it does not end at Benfica. You need to move forward if you want to play on the world stage." But a season with Jose Mourinho, an unbeaten league campaign no less, is hardly a waste.

And Fonseca does not place too much weight on the decision of Roberto Martinez to omit him from the World Cup squad in favour of his Benfica team-mate Tomas Araujo. "The decision of the Portugal head coach does not mean he is not capable," he says.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at the changes at Bournemouth as the club prepares for the Europa League

"Antonio is very capable and is completely ready to play in the Premier League. But it will be a different challenge for him. The challenge in England is week by week, not just waiting for the European games like he could at Benfica. The focus must be there."

Maybe there will be mistakes, lessons to learn even for a 22-year-old player who has already racked up an astonishing 181 appearances for Benfica in all competitions. "In the Premier League, the margin of error is very small. He needs to have that in mind."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of the best bits from Bournemouth's Rayan last season

But the overriding feeling is that this is an opportunity for Silva - and will be a coup for Bournemouth. "Antonio is a very complete centre-back who would help any team in the world. At this moment, it is going to be Bournemouth." A stepping stone to greatness?

"He has all the qualities to make the next move, but he cannot think like that. This move is the most important of his career. He will be in the Premier League. If he wants to move forward, he needs to focus completely and give 100 per cent for Bournemouth."

That is perhaps the lesson of Silva's journey so far. The hype came early. The next step is set to arrive later than expected. But at 22, there remains ample time for him to fulfil the promise that made him one of European football's most coveted young defenders.

Bournemouth have shown repeatedly that they can provide the perfect environment for talented centre-backs to take that next leap. Antonio Silva is now poised to have the opportunity to prove that his journey to the top remains on course. It is simply set to take a different route.

Sports.title: Meet Bahoya... the Bundesliga's fastest player attracting PL interest
Sports.content:
Why Bahoya’s profile is so in-demand

Premier League managers are being forced to come up with new solutions to combat the craze of man-to-man marking that has swept the English top-flight. The challenge is breaking the defensive chain, because once you do, more often than not, chaos ensues.

Having a player with the capacity to consistently beat their man is kryptonite against man-to-man marking. Only four Premier League players completed more take-ons per 90 in the league last season than Bahoya, while only two outperformed him in the Bundesliga.

Jeremy Doku is the gold standard for this metric. The word often associated with the Belgium winger is “unpredictable”, and that is exactly how Bahoya’s U17s coach at Angers describes the 21-year-old.

Like Doku, Bahoya’s unpredictability is not limited to his one-vs-one supremacy. “He can make runs from deep, play between the lines, and wide on the touchline,” Manu Guidicelli tells Sky Sports. “He can go right or left for a dribble – and above all, he can finish the actions.”

Having the capacity to drag your marker into areas of the pitch they do not want to be is another effective method of unlocking man-to-man marking. Guidicelli taught Bahoya how he could exploit his speed advantage in these scenarios at Angers.

“We made him understand he had this ability, and he quickly understood," says Guidicelli, who highlighted Bahoya's footballing IQ as one of his strengths, "and then he scored more goals. When he made those runs from deep, it was hard for defenders to catch up with him."

Asked about Bahoya's acceleration, Dina Ebimbe says: "It's too much. Maybe you can catch him after a while, but at the start, you're definitely not going to see him again. His steps are so quick and he can change direction very fast.”

Winning duels and making interceptions can be an even more effective way of creating an offensive advantage. Bahoya has made this another strength in his game after a lot of work since arriving in Frankfurt.

“He works a lot in the gym,” says Dina Ebimbe. "It changed everything for him because he was too slight when he joined. Everyone pushed him. He was always on the floor. He started work in the gym, and last season we saw his body was really different.”

Bahoya ranked in the top 11 per cent for duels won per 90 (8.9) and top 10 per cent for interceptions per 90 (0.88) among wingers in Europe’s top five leagues last season. His 2.1 tackles per 90 also placed him in the top 13 per cent of that same group.

"Jean-Matteo, in the athletic point, he's really top," says Dina Ebimbe. "He can run and make a lot of sprints. He's one of the fastest players in this league. And now he's becoming stronger."

Sports.title: West Ham in talks for Celtic midfielder Engels
Sports.content:
West Ham are in talks with Celtic over the signing of midfielder Arne Engels.

The 22-year-old also has interest from a number of Premier League clubs. Nottingham Forest saw multiple offers rejected for him on Deadline Day of the winter window.

But it is Championship side West Ham who are currently pursuing the Belgium international, who has two years to run on his contract.

Celtic's chief executive Michael Nicholson said a few weeks ago that the Hoops' transfer activity was proving difficult because they are competing with clubs in the Championship for targets.

Image: Engels has had interest from Premier League clubs this summer

Nicholson was speaking at Celtic's annual general meeting, in which manager Martin O'Neill said his squad was not strong enough to compete and is in major need of signings.

Celtic have since signed striker Kasper Hogh for a club-record fee from Bodo/Glimt.

It remains to be seen if any Premier League clubs will rival West Ham for Engels' signature.

Forest's top midfield target is Lucas Bergvall but they have been unable to strike an agreement with Spurs for the 20-year-old.

Sports.title: Norrie routs Tomic to reach first semi-final of 2026
Sports.content:
Cameron Norrie raced into his first semi-final of 2026 with a 6-1 6-0 thrashing of Bernard Tomic at the Los Cabos Open.

Britain's Norrie had been on a six-match losing streak before arriving in Mexico but has strung together three successive straight-set victories to set up a last-four clash with defending champion Denis Shapovalov.

Tomic, who reached the main draw as a lucky loser from qualifying, held serve in the opening game of the match but then lost the next 12 as Norrie completed the rout in just 50 minutes.

Norrie said: "I'm pleased with the result. I was very solid, I returned well, I made a lot of tough balls when I needed to, and I kept him moving. I enjoyed the match, and it's nice to go to bed a little bit earlier.

"It was a tough one at the French Open. I overtrained a little bit, but good learning. And then I lost a couple of tough matches at Wimbledon and Queen's, and it was a while for me to get my confidence back.

"To get a win here meant a lot. I took a lot of confidence from that and I was just able to play, not thinking about too much, just enjoying myself."

Sports.title: FIFA denies 'selling football' as AFC joins opposition to plan
Sports.content:
FIFA insists "nobody is selling football" amid criticism of its decision to launch a consultation on selling stakes in a World Cup commercial entity to private investors.

However, football's global governing body stopped short of withdrawing the controversial plan and insisted it would press ahead with the consultation period.

UEFA's 55 member associations insisted they would not participate in any FIFA tournament until the plan was withdrawn. CONCACAF, the confederation representing 41 nations from North and Central America, along with the Caribbean, also made clear its opposition to FIFA's plan, saying it "rejected the proposal".

The Asian Football Confederation, representing 47 Asian nations, joined UEFA and CONCACAF in its opposition and called for "FIFA to undertake an urgent review of its governance".

That means confederations representing 143 of FIFA's 211 member associations have now opposed the plan.

In a statement released on Friday morning, FIFA said: "We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

"We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

⁠"Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts."

The statement continued: "FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself.

"Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain."

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has publicly backed the plan, with an investor group led by Thrive Eternal, founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of United States President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner - waiting in the wings to secure a minority stake in the new venture.

However, promises of huge returns to national associations if FFE goes ahead could surely not be honoured if the men's and women's World Cups took place without European involvement, even if Infantino could still muster majority support for FFE.

European and world leagues are also opposed to the plans - fearing that commercial imperatives will drive FIFA to hold bigger and more frequent tournaments in the future, eating even further into domestic schedules.

UEFA's opposition to the plan, in its words, is "unanimous and unequivocal".

"No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership," European football's governing body stated.

FIFA's statement added that "each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future".

The AFC has been a big supporter of Infantino up to now but its intervention marks a shift, with its statement coming close to asking for Infantino to step down. AFC president Sheikh Salman came second behind Infantino in the FIFA presidential election in 2016.

A statement said: "The AFC believes this moment must become a catalyst for strengthening institutional reform. While every FIFA MA must have the opportunity to consider and determine proposals affecting the future of world football, meaningful democracy is not measured solely by the opportunity to vote. It begins with transparent governance, timely consultation, informed deliberation and genuine participation throughout the decision-making process.

"Accordingly, the AFC calls upon FIFA to undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework to ensure that proposals of global significance are developed through proper consultation, meaningful engagement and appropriate oversight by FIFA's statutory bodies."

'Infantino is in a hole and he needs to stop digging

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"It is a desperate, tone-deaf statement that was issued in the middle of the night from FIFA's Zurich bunker. It's very interesting that it doesn't mention their president by name.

"The way I read this is that this is a statement from Gianni Infantino; it's not necessarily a FIFA statement. How many people inside FIFA actually agree with what he is doing?

"He's in a hole and he needs to stop digging. He needs to start reading the room. He needs to start accepting the fact his power is starting to ebb away and he needs to start by apologising to football, to football fans all around the world - and he also needs to start apologising and explain himself to the confederations and the presidents of the 211 member associations.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh's update after UEFA confirmed it will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with his proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup

"And he needs to stop blaming the media. What is this crazy obsession he's got? He seems to have picked it up from President Donald Trump, where he thinks it's a good idea to keep lashing out at the media. He seems to somehow think that is going to help him.

"The reporting that has been done this week, which was led by The Times and the Financial Times has been completely and utterly accurate. And if it wasn't for this reporting, there wouldn't be this furore that we have now and we wouldn't know the facts we know now.

"I suggest Infantino needs to change course. He needs to wake up and fully understand the mess he has created for himself and he needs to start saying sorry because I think that's the only way he's going to be able to save himself."

Is there a way out for Infantino?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh explains how FIFA president Infantino is losing support - and analyses who could potentially take over as FIFA president

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"Infantino has been in plenty of tight spots and he has managed to extricate from them. But I think he's in big, big trouble now. I think this is the biggest crisis he's faced - and it's all of his own making.

"The best way for him to survive, he seems to think, is to pretend this is all just a democratic process, what's happening now is just a consultation, the 211 FAs can decide whether to go ahead with this plan, and if they don't, no problem at all, it's all been a storm in a teacup.

"Other people, I think, would advise him to come out and say sorry, then lie low for a while, maybe ride it out and maybe he could be re-elected as FIFA president unopposed next March, but that doesn't seem to be what he's doing.

"I'm not sure he can carry on down this road of blaming the media and carrying on with the consultation process. I'm not sure he understands the strength of feeling against him - not just over this, but over lots of things he's done since he's been FIFA president."

Sports.title: Fowler, Cantlay impress as Malnati leads after threatening 59 round
Sports.content:
Rickie Fowler and Patrick Cantlay are in contention after the first round of the Rocket Classic in Detroit as leader Peter Malnati threatened a sensational sub-60 score.

Malnati shot a career-best nine-under 61 to tie the tournament's record for the first round to take a two-shot lead over Fowler and Ryan Gerard, with Cantlay and Patrick Fishburn another shot back.

When Malnati stood on the first tee, his caddie suggested leaving the driver in his bag to play it safe and set up a solid start.

Malnati, though, went against the advice and used his driver to put a tee shot in the middle of the fairway that set up his first of seven birdies on the front nine.

"Even in the beginning before I knew it was going to be a special day, I didn't feel the same level of like anxiety," he said.

"I don't think I took advantage of a super easy course. I played great."

Image: Peter Malnati hits from the 18th tee during the first round of the Rocket Classic (AP Photo/Jose Juarez)

With thoughts of a sub-60 round crossing his mind, he made a 55-foot putt for birdie at the 11th and was nine under through 13 holes before missing some putts down the stretch in a bogey-free round.

Detroit Golf Club underwent a $16 million renovation, including converting a couple of par-5 holes into par-4s and adding a lot of bunkers, in an attempt to restore Donald Ross' vision for it more than a century ago, while making it more challenging.

Fowler and Ryan Gerard shot 63s, putting them two shots back and one stroke ahead of Cantlay and Fishburn.

Michael Brennan surged up the leaderboard after starting two over through four holes with eight straight birdies - one shy of the PGA Tour record.

He finished with a 65, putting him four strokes back with a pack of players that includes Keegan Bradley, who appeared to be mocked by some spectators who pretended he hit a hole in one on the par-three fifth.

Open runner-up Cameron Young has work to do on one under while US Open champion Wyndham Clark is on one over.

Despite significant changes at the course, Malnati and many other players still went low at a tournament that has been a birdie fest since 2019, when a Detroit-based mortgage company ended a decade-long drought in Michigan without a PGA Tour stop that dated to Tiger Woods winning the last Buick Open.

The PGA Tour is moving to a new model for 2028, effectively creating two tours, and Detroit organizers are taking an exit. The Rocket Classic wasn't interested in continuing to spend $15 million a year to be part of the second tier and didn't want to double the costs to be part of the elite tier.

"It's definitely been a bummer to kind of come into this knowing it was the last one," said Fowler, a Rocket Mortgage spokesman and the tournament's 2023 champion.
