Sports.title: Franco Baresi dead at 66: AC Milan legend passes away with club sharing heartbreaking tribute to one of football's best ever defenders
Sports.content:
Franco Baresi dead at 66: AC Milan legend passes away with club sharing heartbreaking tribute to one of football's best ever defenders

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

AC Milan and Italy legend Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, his former club confirmed on Friday.

The one-club man was synonymous with the red-and-black side of the San Siro, playing every minute of his 20-year career for il Rossoneri.

As such, there was no shortage of emotion in the club's statement shared in the early hours of Friday morning, as AC Milan extended support not just to Baresi's family, but to their entire community.

'The entire history of AC Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi,' the statement read. 'His example and integrity will be forever etched into the Club's DNA, just as his iconic number 6 shirt is.

'The condolences AC Milan extends to Franco Baresi's family at such a difficult time are shared by every Rossonero, who feels this loss as their own.'

The defender, long considered one of the best of all time, served as captain for 14 years, and helped Milan claim six Serie A titles and three European Cups among numerous other honours.

Italian football legend Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, his former club confirmed

The heavily decorated defender dedicated the duration of his career to his boyhood club

In 1999, Baresi's feats in club colours won him AC Milan's Player of the Century award.

The player known as 'Piscinin' also won the World Cup with Italy in 1982, later coming heartbreakingly close to claiming a second when the Azzurri reached the final in 1994 before defeat to Brazil on penalties.

Just hours before sharing the tragic news, AC Milan were forced to deny rumours on Wednesday that Baresi had died, after the player was admitted to hospital in Milan.

Italian outlet Tuttosport had broken the 'news', which prompted tributes from football fans including Italy's deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini.

Baresi had previously undergone lung surgery in August 2025 to remove a pulmonary nodule, and later was treated with cancer-prevention immunotherapy.

His last public appearance came touchingly at the San Siro, as he and his great friend - and former Inter Milan rival - Beppe Bergomi walked into the iconic stadium bearing the Olympic flame during the Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony earlier this year.

Baresi had initially been rejected by Inter Milan's academy as a junior player, after being deemed too small and frail for the rigorous demands of 1970s football, with his eventual rivals instead taking on his elder brother Giuseppe.

That twist of fate brought Baresi to Milan's academy, and he would go on to make his debut for the senior team at the age of 17 - after being given his nickname by the club's masseur at the time, Paolo Mariconti, which means 'little one' in Milanese dialect.

Baresi donned the captain's armband for Italy's second tilt at the World Cup in 1994, after winning the trophy in 1982

His trophy haul with il Rossoneri contains three European Cups, six Serie A titles, and countless other honours

His last public appearance came poignantly at the San Siro where he acted as a torchbearer in the Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony

Beppe Baresi was later made Inter captain, with the pair regularly exchanging pennants during the Milan derbies of the 1980s.

Inter shared their own touching statement to one of their bitterest competitive rivals, writing: 'Farewell to Franco Baresi, protagonist of the great clashes in the Milan Derby and one of the figures who most defined the history of the rivalry.

'Captain, team man, and flag bearer of AC Milan, he lived every matchup with Inter between competition and respect, within a challenge that wrote unforgettable pages of Italian soccer.

'President Giuseppe Marotta and all of FC Internazionale Milano stand in solidarity with the Baresi family, brother Beppe, and AC Milan in this moment of grief.'

Baresi stuck with AC Milan throughout the match-fixing Totonero scandal which saw the club relegated in 1980, and a second relegation in 1982, before going on to see Milan through their heavily decorated glory years under legendary managers Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello.

His role as the bedrock in Milan's all-Italian defence saw him written into the club's legend, and in 1989, named Ballon d'Or runner-up.

His defensive partner Paolo Maldini shared his grief in a touching statement on Friday, calling Baresi 'the strongest player' he had ever 'had the honour' to play alongside.

'Ciao Franco,' his statement began. 'Today I feel the same feeling when, for whatever reason, you couldn't go on the field next to us: "what will we do without our Captain?"

'You taught me to fight until my last breath, what does sticking to the shirt mean and the value of being a true leader. You did it by example, every day: few words, but lots of facts.

'You protected me as a child, guided me as a boy and inspired me as a man. You were the strongest football player I have ever had the honor to play with.

'A loving hug to your whole family, especially to your wife and your children. We'll miss you, Captain. But the light of your star will continue to shine on us forever.'

Italy's greatest ever defender Paolo Maldini shared a heartbreaking tribute to his former team-mate (pictured at a Legends match in 2012)

In 2020, Baresi was named as the club's honorary vice-president, and he continued to be enmeshed in Milan's culture, attending matches at the San Siro when possible.

Baresi is also thought to have even hoped to visit Milan's pre-season training camp at Milanello earlier this month, but was unable to due to his ill health.

After retiring from football in 1997, Milan retired his No 6 shirt, and after a brief stint as director of Fulham, Baresi returned to the club to coach their youth ranks until 2006.

Tributes from other Serie A sides began to pour in shortly after the news broke, with Juventus honouring his 'class and leadership'.

'There are people who, with their talent, enter history. And others who, with their humanity, remain there forever. Franco Baresi was both,' the statement read. 'Class, style, leadership, and respect on and off the field.

'An example for generations of players and fans, loved and admired by all football enthusiasts. His memory will live on forever. Juventus Football Club stands in solidarity with the Baresi family and AC Milan in this moment of profound sorrow.'

The president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) Giovanni Malago added: 'Italian football has lost one of its legends, an extraordinary champion who wore only two jerseys throughout his career: AC Milan and the Azzurri.

'A romantic choice, which has rightfully won him a place in the hearts of fans and millions of Italians. We will remember him as he deserves during the national team's upcoming matches, the national team for which he has always demonstrated exceptional dedication, becoming one of its most glorious symbols.'

Jamie Carragher shared his own tribute, with the Liverpool defender singling out Baresi as one of the 'all time greats'.

'It’s always a sad day for football when one of the all time greats pass away, and that’s exactly what Franco Baresi was,' Carragher shared on X. 'I’ve always seen him as the greatest centre back I ever saw & the ultimate one club man. RIP Capitano'.

Sports.title: Sandro Tonali reveals why he chose Tottenham over Man City in just 10 minutes, how he already has a 'mini connection' with Roberto De Zerbi and how he fought for the 'best deal for Newcastle' before £100m switch
Sports.content:
Sandro Tonali reveals why he chose Tottenham over Man City in just 10 minutes, how he already has a 'mini connection' with Roberto De Zerbi and how he fought for the 'best deal for Newcastle' before £100m switch

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Our interview with Sandro Tonali is over, but as we shake hands, we have a small correction to make with Tottenham Hotspur’s £100million summer signing.

Earlier on in the conversation, Tonali had explained how nice it was that he was now getting to speak in Italian – with his new manager Roberto De Zerbi and his assistants and team-mates such as Guglielmo Vicario and Destiny Udogie – after three years of only using English at Newcastle United.

Except, as those of us from the heart of the North East will tell you, we do not talk in English. We speak Geordie, and to Tonali’s credit, he appreciates the difference. He tells us how he grew to love the locals who supported him around St James’ Park, and explains how he wanted his old club to feel like they were getting their money’s worth once it became clear that he would be leaving this summer.

‘The first thing was to get the best deal for Newcastle,’ Tonali says when discussing his decision to leave his former side managed by Eddie Howe, whose exit from Newcastle was coincidentally revealed on the same day as we spoke in Sydney.

‘I met there some of the best people for football. They love football. They live for football. When I decided to move, I said to my agent and to Ross Wilson (Newcastle’s sporting director) that I wanted the best deal for Newcastle because they deserve everything. This is football. Sometimes you have to understand how everything can change in your life in five minutes.'

Newcastle are in bother this summer. Not only might Bruno Guimaraes follow Tonali and Anthony Gordon out of the door at St James' Park, they have lost Howe now also. Tonali can only speak for himself, and he explains it was simply time for a change after three seasons and speaking with his family.

Sandro Tonali needed only a few minutes to convince him that Tottenham was his ideal Premier League destination

While sitting inside a makeshift boardroom set up inside Tottenham’s team hotel near the Sydney Harbour Bridge, Tonali explains how it was an easy decision to choose Spurs over others interested.

The £100m asking price that Newcastle placed on him influenced his options as he and his family were initially interested in returning to Italy. But they soon realised those in Serie A could not afford his services.

‘We stayed three years in Newcastle and after three years, we spoke all together, me and my family,’ Tonali says. 'It was impossible for the money (to return to Italy). For the salary, you can speak all the time, but if you don’t find the money for the transfer, you don’t have the chance to move.

'England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness, for my family. I spoke with two teams. I understood after 10, 15 minutes that Tottenham would be my next team.’

Manchester City were believed to be the other club in for Tonali, who has won 32 caps for the Italian national team at 26 years old. He is rather liking the Little Italy connection developing within Tottenham now as he tells us: ‘After the last season, I spoke with my wife. We wanted to change our life. Not just for the city. We wanted to change everything. We spoke with two clubs.

‘When we spoke with Tottenham, we decided to sign for this team. They spoke with 100 per cent passion, 100 per cent seriousness. For this city, for my life outside of football for my family, OK, it’s like 10 per cent. Roberto and the director made the difference to the deal.

'I spoke after two minutes with my wife and my family and I said, “Probably it will be one of my best decisions of my career”. She told me, “You have 100 per cent the control over this decision”. I wanted to speak with her because it’s our life.

‘Roberto said the project will be tough but will be perfect for me, for you, for the city, an we can do one of the best seasons because we have big players. We just have to put a lot of work in.’

Alongside Tonali, Spurs have also spent £85m on signing Mateus Fernandes on West Ham, to complete their midfield. On officially being a £100m footballer, Tonali says: ‘You have to understand that this is football. The price is different now to 10 years ago. I know I have a lot of pressure but I know I’m a football player, I know my responsibilities, I know this team, I know the people here. I have to play like I’m a normal player, a normal Tottenham player, with passion, putting my energy in every day. It’s not £1m, £10m, or £100m. You just have to be a passionate player for this gaffer.’

Tonali previously spent a decade in Italy with Brescia, De Zerbi’s hometown. He and the Spurs boss have this ‘mini connection’, as Tonali describes it, and they previously met up there. ‘We spoke about him, about his work, about the passion that he puts into every single moment with the team for this work and I think now, after two weeks, I know everything is real,’ Tonali adds. ‘All gaffers are different. I passed three years with Eddie and he was fantastic, especially for me. But now I’ve found a different gaffer who works a lot on the pitch, a lot with the tactics, a lot with the ball. We love to play with the ball because we are a big team with big players.’

Sports.title: 'I stayed up for England vs Mexico - then fell asleep at half-time!': Cole Palmer on World Cup heartache, feeling fresh after seven-week summer holiday and his bromance with new team-mate Morgan Rogers
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer is talking his ‘cold’ celebration and whether he will allow his best friend in football and new team-mate, Morgan Rogers, to continue to use it after scoring at Chelsea.

It is technically his, after all, as per the register for the Intellectual Property Office.

‘I’ve trademarked it so if he tries to do anything, he’ll have the bailiffs at his door,’ Palmer tells us, prompting a fair few laughs from the journalists interviewing him in Sydney, Australia.

It is a classic Palmer line, delivered nonchalantly as we sit down with this 24-year-old at the training ground of local side Sydney FC, and he continues: ‘Nah, we’ll do it together, I think.

‘We've never actually spoke about it. He does it. I do it. I always speak to him but when I heard Chelsea were trying to sign him, I was texting him even more.

‘He was probably sick of me but at least he’s here now! Morgs told me straightaway when he was coming. It didn’t get leaked. Nobody knew. Just me and him and the higher people at the club.

Cole Palmer says he will share his 'cold' celebration with new team-mate Morgan Rogers

The Chelsea star is glad to have his boyhood friend alongside him going into the new season

‘So it was a difficult secret to keep, but I kept it! Everyone knows how good he is. Obviously he’s one of my best friends so I’m very happy about it.

‘We’re two different players. He’s more physical than me, on and off the ball. He likes to drive with it. I like to play passes. I think we can play well together, and we played together when we were young (in the academy of Manchester City).’

Palmer is speaking for the first time since Rogers signed from Aston Villa for £117million – he describes it as a ‘next-level’ buy by Chelsea – and since he missed out on making Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the summer’s World Cup. Without him, his country reached the semi-finals, where they were beaten by Argentina.

‘If someone told you that you're essentially not good enough to get in the squad, then you’re going to think, like, alright, whatever then, try to go that extra bit harder,’ Palmer says when asked whether he is carrying some extra motivation into the next season.

‘I watched some of it (the World Cup). Obviously I was away and the times were a bit mad in America. It was a bit difficult. But I did watch.’

Did he manage to stay up to watch England v Mexico in the round of 16? ‘Yeah,’ he says of that 2am kick-off in the UK. ‘But then I fell asleep at half-time.’

A summer break was not the worst news for Chelsea, selfishly. It allowed Palmer a chance to rest, recover, and reset after having not had any off-season for a few years. In 2025, he had the Club World Cup. In 2024, he had the Euros. In 2023, he was at the Under 21 Euros.

Is he itching to return to the England fold after Tuchel’s snub, however?

He had seven weeks off and reveals that he fell asleep at half-time of England vs Mexico

Chelsea are on tour in Australia and face Tottenham in Sydney on Saturday

‘I’m not really thinking about that now, to be honest,’ Palmer adds. ‘I’m just looking forward to the season with Chelsea, and to be honest, I’m not too bothered about that.

‘My summer was great. I had like seven weeks off or summit. Which I’ve never really had. It was good. I went on holiday with my family and that. I feel fresh.

‘It was strange. I didn’t know where to go. I went on holiday and was thinking, “Where do I go next?” Checking when I was back in. To be fair, I got bored after like six weeks. I was sat in Marbella thinking, “I want to go back in”, and I never thought I’d think that!’

Palmer’s new manager at Chelsea, Xabi Alonso, spoke to him during his seven weeks of downtime in the summer. ‘When I got told I wasn’t going to the World Cup, I think he knew, so he messaged me,’ Palmer says. ‘I can't remember what he said. I think he said don't worry about it or whatever. Normal stuff. It was nice. Him and his staff have been good, a breath of fresh air with his ideas.’

Palmer’s 2025-26 campaign, in which Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League to miss out on any form of European football, was disrupted by a groin injury.

He is not used to being sidelined or unable to freely act like his ‘cold’ self, and that was hard.

‘I didn’t really know how to deal with it,’ Palmer explains. ‘The first few months, with me being injured, I just wanted to go out and play. Which I probably shouldn’t have done.

‘Obviously I couldn’t play how I wanted to play. It was a bad season personally with injuries and stuff but I feel good now. The seven weeks obviously helped. I’m ready to go again.’

Palmer also reveals for the first time how he considered turning to surgery at the time, as he sought expert advice in Scandinavia, saying: ‘Yeah, I went to Sweden or Denmark, one of those countries, to see a doctor. We did speak about it. But I didn't end up getting it.’

Now that he feels fit again, Alonso has told him what he wants from him. ‘We spoke,’ Palmer says. ‘He sees me in the No 10, in the pockets, close to the striker, so we’ll see. When you sign good players, obviously your team is going to be better. It should be a good season.’

Sports.title: Next stop... Paris? Diamond Necklace could thrill French fans after sparkling in Goodwood sunshine - and your three best bets for day four
Sports.content:
Diamond Necklace sparkled in the Goodwood sunshine to land the Group 1 Qatar Nassau Stakes and could be poised to strut her stuff in Paris this autumn.

Aidan O’Brien’s filly extended her unbeaten career record to six with a routine two-and-three-quarter-length defeat of Friendly Soul under Ryan Moore, encouraging her handler to dream of a tilt at the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe in October.

O’Brien said: ‘Diamond Necklace is a lovely filly who has danced every dance. This was up to a mile and a quarter against older fillies, so we did not really know what was going to happen, but we wanted to put on pace to find out.

‘She has options now, whether she stays at a mile and a quarter and goes to the fillies’ race in France, or to Leopardstown or an Arc trial. She is a great cruiser and progressing well.

Diamond Necklace pulls clear at Goodwood to win the Qatar Nassau Stakes

SAM'S DAY 4 TIPS... 15.00 – Cerulean Bay each-way The loveable Cerulean Bay will be written off by many given he tackles this highly competitive handicap off a career high mark. That is an understandable take, but the profile of this race has changed a little in recent years with many of the lightly-raced three-year-olds which used to frequent this contest sold to race abroad. Although Cerulean Bay has been around a while he is only five and he returns to the South Downs looking to defend an unbeaten 2-2 record at the track so appeals as a sporting each-way play with Colin Keane booked. 15.35 – Jakajaro There wouldn’t be many quicker horses in training than Jakajaro and he may put that blistering early speed to good use in this exciting renewal. Trainer Robert Cowell is adept at finding improvement with maturing sprinters and the five-year-old has taken his form to another level this term, including when a fine third in a Group 2 event at the Curragh last time when the climb to the line found him out late on. This downhill track should play to his strengths ideally and he should go close to landing this for his owners who love a winner at this meeting. 6.10 Naqeeb each-way The son of Nathaniel has been a superb flagbearer for Julie Camacho and Steve Brown and it was agonising for the Yorkshire-based training operation that their versatile six-year-old was beaten a short-head in a Listed affair at today’s venue back in May. That narrow defeat meant his track stats now read 212 and the selection ran right up to his best in the Summer Mile at Ascot last time when a creditable fifth to Zeus Olympios, a race which has already thrown up a win for runner-up Holloway Bay.

‘It is possible (the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe). I do not know how far we ask her to go, and it will depend on everything, but the next run will tell us where she is going to go after that.

Moore was equally enthusiastic about the daughter of St Mark’s Basilica: ‘That is the best Diamond Necklace has felt. She is improving with her racing.

‘I think 10 furlongs is probably her optimum, but with those classy horses, they do everything right, so there is a chance she would stay further.’

The combination recorded a double in the Markel Richmond Stakes when it proved more of a case of punters’ best friend than Man’s Best Friend with Moore steering the popular 11/2 chance to success in the Group 2 event.

The victory looked in doubt for much of the contest as the colt’s rider struggled to find a clear passage aboard the Ballydoyle-trained son of No Nay Never.

However, once in the clear the duo flew past the admirable Adaay Of Scarlett to score by a snug length and give his trainer a first win in the race since 2000.

If it’s not one O’Brien winning, it’s another and Aidan’s son Joseph got in on the action courtesy of the progressive Enceladus in the Group 3 Gordon Stakes.

The winner of Royal Ascot’s King George V Handicap took the step up to Group company in his stride, finding plenty for pressure from the furlong marker under Dylan Browne McMonagle to comfortably hold the challenge of Geryon by a length and a quarter.

Asked about stepping up in trip for the St Leger, Browne McMonagle said: ‘I am sure the distance will be no problem for him, but he is not short of gears either; he has plenty of gears for a mile and a half.

‘I think as he develops, it will be no problem going up in trip, which will open up options for him going forwards.’

Billy Loughnane, hero of day two for his exploits on Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes winner Bow Echo, came crashing back down to earth, quite literally, when his first-race ride Savvy Disco dramatically clipped heels at the furlong marker and came down.

Thankfully, both horse and jockey were absolutely fine and none the worse for the experience, so much so that Loughnane rose from the canvas to partner Avalon Queen to victory in the seven furlong maiden.

Over at Galway, Daniel King became the first jockey in 42 years to win both the Plate and the Hurdle when Putapoundinthejar followed hard on the heels of success for King Alexander 24 hours beforehand.

Sports.title: Kate O'Connor ready for next challenge after golden breakthrough
Sports.content:
Kate O'Connor ready for next challenge after golden breakthrough

Kate O'Connor became Northern Ireland's first Commonwealth track and field champion in 40 years before setting her sights on another major title this summer.

View Image Kate O'Connor secured Northern Ireland's first Commonwealth athletics gold in 40 years.

Kate O’Connor rewrote the history books but is keen to add another chapter to another storied summer before next month is out.

The absence of two-time world champion Katarina Johnson-Thompson from the Commonwealth Games heptathlon made O'Connor the one to beat, a new feeling for the Northern Irish athlete.

Her silver medal at last year's World Championships in Tokyo underlined her potential, but there's winning on paper and winning in practice.

She's the first Northern Ireland team member to win gold here, the first track and field athlete to top the podium in 40 years and the first woman to do so since Dame Mary Peters in 1974.

And while the emotion of her first major senior championship title came in a blur, there won't be long to reset her focus before the European Championships in Birmingham in just 13 days.

A rested Johnson-Thompson, who prioritised that event over Glasgow, awaits, along with Swiss star Annik Kälin and others in a stacked field. Triple Olympic and European champion Nafissatou Thiam is not competing as she continues a cautious comeback from injury.

O'Connor's winning score of 6,569 points at Scotstoun was well short of Kälin's world-leading 6,819, but the 25-year-old didn't just have to battle the new pressures of expectation here – she also had to contend with the elements. At times it didn't just rain; it was biblical.

"I came here wanting to score somewhere in the 6,700s, or even higher, because I felt I was in that kind of shape," she said.

"My coaches reminded me that championships aren't about big scores – they're about competing. You have to deal with whatever conditions you're given, and with the rain and cold I think I produced a very good score. Hopefully at the Europeans in Birmingham it'll be warmer and I'll have another chance to chase that bigger total.

"I'm not worried about the turnaround before Birmingham. I'll just treat these last few days as really good training.

"It's not a difficult journey home and my body feels good. I feel healthy and I don't think I emptied the tank out there, so I'm looking forward to what's next.

"Being one of the favourites was a completely new experience for me. Last year I learned what it was like to carry the expectation of being in medal contention, but this was the first time I'd gone into a championships as someone people expected to win gold. That brings a different kind of pressure."

O'Connor finished eighth in 2018 and claimed silver behind Johnson-Thompson four years later in Birmingham.

But it was only last year that her life changed: pentathlon silver and bronze at the World and European Indoor Championships, gold at the World University Games and that famous silver in Tokyo.

Records and personal bests were rewritten and then rewritten again, with her Irish national record of 6,714 points meaning she ended the season ranked second in the world.

Article continues below

After admitting her frustration with her opening day, she recorded a solid leap of 1.82m in the high jump, a season's best 52.85m in the javelin and won the concluding 800m at a canter. Her winning margin over England's silver medallist Jade O'Dowda was a huge 291 points.

"As an athlete you're always looking ahead to the next competition, so you don't always stop to appreciate what you've achieved," she added. "Hearing those things makes you realise just how special it is.”

Sports.title: Relay silver ends Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Glasgow campaign
Sports.content:
Relay silver ends Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Glasgow campaign

Adam Ramsay-Peaty ended his Commonwealth Games campaign with relay silver before turning his attention to next month's European Championships.

View Image Adam Ramsay-Peaty helped England to mixed 4x100m medley relay silver.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty waved goodbye to the Commonwealth Games with a silver medal as he looks for a quick reset ahead of the European Championships.

‌



Ramsay-Peaty teamed up with Ollie Morgan, Ed Mildred, and Jacob Peters for mixed 4x100m medley relay silver to bring his medal haul from Glasgow 2026 to three.

‌



His pair of individual bronzes and a relay silver would not have been what he had envisioned at the start of the Games, but Ramsay-Peaty leaves Glasgow with a new mindset after making his return to major championships.

‌



The 31-year-old has become used to no longer being invincible but still has the hunger to get back to the top for Los Angeles 2028.

That starts with the European Championships in Paris next month and Ramsay-Peaty knows he faces a race against time to improve on his Glasgow showings.

“It's been a learning curve,” he said. “The Commonwealth Games has always been one of those that challenged me for some reason or another.

‌



“I'm really looking forward to Europeans. We have got a lot of work to do with these next 10 days to have that shift because the way I see it is that we have fallen short by a few percent.

“We compound those two percents, and silvers turn into bronzes and bronzes turn into fourths. That's just the reality.

“We have got the cohesion in the team, we have got the experience in the team to turn around the ship very quick. It’s a two-year project.

‌



I think the whole team would agree that we have probably had a tough look at where we are on that leaderboard. Scotland's ahead of us as well, and we're meant to be having that depth in England. We've got to obviously look at why.

“We won’t have a full debrief but just a quick one to say, okay, how do we turn this around for Europeans?

“I'll almost have to forget the experience I've had this week in my personal situation and learn from it very quickly.”

Sports.title: World Cup winner Franco Baresi dies aged 66 as tributes flood in for Italy and AC Milan icon
Sports.content:
Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, as the world of football mourns one of Italy's greatest-ever talents. The Travagilato-born star will be remembered for a trophy-laden 20-year career with AC Milan, as well as a sensational international career culminating in winning the 1982 World Cup.

A statement from I Rossoneri confirming the news of Baresi's passing on Friday read: "Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan, is incredibly difficult. But everyone at the Club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi's memory.

"We must be strong and gather every bit of energy, even at this saddest of times. We lost Franco only a few months after his last public appearance in a packed San Siro, at the Milan Winter Olympics opening ceremony, an event on the world stage he helped make unforgettable.

Vinicius Jr set to STAY at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest as Jose Mourinho pulls rank READ MORE :

Ruben Amorim admits to Man Utd mistakes and explains how sacking has changed him READ MORE :

"In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he'll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever."

‌



A number of other Serie A clubs have also paid tribute to Baresi in a showing of solidarity with AC Milan, as well as the former centre-half's family and friends. Juventus wrote: "There are people who, with their talent, enter history. And others who, with their humanity, remain there forever.

"Franco Baresi was both. Class, style, leadership, and respect on and off the field. An example for generations of players and fans, loved and admired by all football enthusiasts.

"His memory will live on forever. Juventus Football Club stands in solidarity with the Baresi family and @acmilan in this moment of profound sorrow."

View 4 Images Franco Baresi has died at 66 (Image: -Birmingham Post and Mail)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lazio added: "S.S. Lazio joins the family's mourning for the passing of Franco Baresi, the unforgettable defensive bastion of the Italian National Team and of Milan."

Napoli wrote: "President Aurelio De Laurentiis, Mr. Allegri, the executives, and all of SSC Napoli express their deepest condolences for the passing of Franco Baresi, a flag and legend of Milan and of the entire panorama of Italian football. To his family, the sincerest closeness from the entire Azzurri club."

Roma said: "AS Roma joins in the mourning for the passing of Franco Baresi, who with his career left an indelible mark on the history of football. The Club stands in solidarity with the grief of his family and loved ones."

‌



Genoa, meanwhile, added: "The Club joins the grief of the family, the world of football, and @acmilan for the passing of Franco Baresi, pillar and legend of world football. Rest in peace, Franco."

One of world football's most influential players, Baresi enjoyed a remarkable 20-year club career with AC Milan between 1977 and 1997. With I Rossoneri, he won eight league titles, four Supercoppa Italianas and a trilogy of European Cups.

View 4 Images AC Milan retired Franco Baresi's shirt (Image: AC Milan via Getty Images)

View 4 Images Franco Baresi enjoyed a trophy-laden career (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

‌



Baresi also managed 81 appearances for the Italian national football team, and was instrumental to the nation's success at the 1982 World Cup. In the final of that tournament, which took place in Spain, Italy ran out 3-1 winners over West Germany to secure their third title in FIFA's most prestigious international tournament.

After a career which is best described as legendary, AC Milan made the executive decision to retire Baresi's iconic shirt number of six when he called time on playing. He was the first player to receive the honour in the club's history.

Paolo Maldini is the only other player to have a shirt retired by I Rossoneri, after enjoying a similarly astonishing career to Baresi.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford pundit agreement emerges as audacious swap deal involving £51million man proposed
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford pundit agreement emerges as audacious swap deal involving £51million man proposed

Marcus Rashford has been linked with a move away from Manchester United and club icons have shared their thoughts on the forward's future

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford spent last season away from Manchester United on loan (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Two Manchester United icons have argued that Marcus Rashford should spend next season at Old Trafford. The England international has spent time on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona since his last appearance for the club in December 2024.

‌



Rashford scored and assisted 14 goals apiece during his successful stint at Barcelona, helping the club win La Liga last term. However, the Catalan club opted not to trigger their £26million buy option, leaving the forward’s future uncertain.

‌



The 28-year-old openly expressed his desire to remain at the Camp Nou permanently but Barcelona have since added Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi to their frontline. A separate £40m clause, available to any club except Liverpool or Manchester City, has also now expired.

‌



It has since been claimed that Rashford could be used as a makeweight to help United sign Roma’s Manu Kone. Italian publication Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Kone is valued at around £51m and Roma would benefit from adding Rashford to their squad, though his wages would force the club to pursue a loan move, which is deemed unlikely.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rashford is currently set to return to United training this summer, more than 18 months after falling out of favour under former United boss Ruben Amorim. However, Michael Carrick's move into the dugout has led two club icons to believe there is an opportunity for Rashford to revive his United career next season.

‌



Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

Former midfielder Paul Ince believes Rashford would respond well to playing under Carrick, with the pair having previously been United teammates and also working together during the manager’s earlier coaching roles at Old Trafford. "I think Carrick can get the best out of him. I really, really do," Ince told Oddschecker.

"If Carrick just puts his arm around him and says, 'Yeah, listen, you know, I want you at the club, I need you at the club. This is where you’re going to play. This is what you’re going to do.' Then I believe you’re going to see a very, very good Rashford for Manchester United."

Ince’s thoughts are echoed by former United defender Wes Brown. The five-time Premier League winner is confident that Carrick would welcome Rashford back into his squad, given what the former Barcelona loanee can add to his attack.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick and Rashford were previously teammates at United (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

“I’m sure Michael Carrick would love him back because it gives him another option,” Brown told The Sun on behalf of LiveFootballTickets. “If he could come into the scene this season, that helps out massively.

“I’m still not sure what’s going to happen, but I think if it was just up to Michael, he would definitely be back in. Obviously Marcus would have loved to have probably stayed at Barca.

‌



“They went another way, so I’m not sure what other options there is really. For me, it’s always time. People always fall out and you can always rekindle things in football. It’s just the way it is. I think it’ll be a boost for Michael for him to be here next season.”

Rashford has two years remaining on his United contract. The forward has made 426 appearances for his boyhood club, scoring 138 goals and registering 79 assists.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe gets England job verdict as Thomas Tuchel stance taken after Newcastle bombshell
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Eddie Howe gets England job verdict as Thomas Tuchel stance taken after Newcastle bombshell

Eddie Howe is out of work after deciding to leave Newcastle just weeks before the new season starts and the former Bournemouth boss has been linked with the England job

View 4 Images Eddie Howe is likely to have plenty of interest when he decides to return to management (Image: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock)

Former England striker Emile Heskey believes Eddie Howe would be perfect for the Three Lions job if Thomas Tuchel left his post at St George's Park. However, he backs Tuchel to take the national team forward and learn from any mistakes that cost them in the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

‌



Englishman Howe has surprisingly ended his five-year spell at Newcastle United just under three weeks before the new Premier League season kicks off on August 21. The North East side have endured a torrid time recently with their best players poached amid the club's battle to meet their financial fair play requirements.

‌



Star striker Alexander Isak completed a British-record £125million switch to Liverpool last summer. That has been followed in recent months by the departures of winger Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur.

‌



Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players READ MORE :

Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier READ MORE :

Now, fan-favourite Bruno Guimaraes has been the latest player to be linked with a St James' Park departure. Arsenal are reportedly set to make a £70m offer for the Brazilian midfielder, in what would be another huge blow to Newcastle.

And Heskey, who starred for Liverpool, Aston Villa and several other clubs during his career, has now shared his view on the chaos at Newcastle as he speaks exclusively to Mirror Football on Howe's shock exit.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"It's obviously not great for the players, not great for the club," Heskey said. "I think he would have seen something and looked at how far he's brought them, and he's done a fantastic job to bring them to where he's brought them, but there is a ceiling, I think, within the club.

"And then missing out on transfers and not being able to get the players that he wants, and still having to try and push for Champions League, still trying to push for more and more.

"I think he's just probably looked at it and said he's taken them as far as you possibly can within the confines of financial fair play and what the club can actually do.

‌



"He's done a fantastic job, to be honest. He's won a trophy and that's one of the things that the club would have put on him and he's done that."

View 4 Images Eddie Howe has walked away from Newcastle United (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

The 48-year-old has previously been linked with the England job after earning admirers for his work at Newcastle and Bournemouth. Howe has also worked with FA chief football officer Dan Ashworth at St James' Park.

‌



"The reality is that he's the best fit," Heskey admits. "When you're looking at an English manager with the best CV and the most experience. The only thing is, it's one thing being a club manager when you're so used to being with the players 24/7, moulding them into what you want.

"Then you're bringing them all from different places and trying to integrate them and get them to play the way that you want within 10 days. It's very tough. He will have some time off because I don't think Tuchel's going anywhere too soon.

"If you're looking at club management, I would have definitely said Chelsea would have been a decent fit before they got [Xabi] Alonso. I think he does really well with younger players.

‌



"He pushes them and drives them to do the best and not rest on their laurels. A lot of young lads, can at times rest on their laurels: 'We've done good, we've had one good game.' No, he will be pushing them. It's not one good game. It's a whole career. He's definitely one of those who will push them."

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

Newcastle are expected to appoint Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle as Howe's successor. The German has a huge task to restore the Magpies' confidence before their season opener at home to Liverpool on August 23.

‌



"There was so much promise when the owners came in because they've got so much money to spend, but they can't spend the money," Heskey said. "You've got to balance the books and balancing the books means actually selling some of your best players.

"Aston Villa are in a similar boat. They're having to sell so many of the best young players; you don't really want to sell them, but it's just to balance the books. That's the tough side of it, where you're sitting there with an owner that wants to buy players, wants to invest money, but just can't do it.

"They've got a really huge fan base up there. They get their stadium rocking, but they just can't spend the money that they would want to do to challenge with the top four. Become the force that [Manchester] City are.

‌



"It's difficult to say where they will be this season. Mid-table will probably be good. When you're just losing all your best players, mid-table is probably going to be your best ask.

"It's gonna be tough and it's going to be a lot of pressure on some of these young lads, and it's sad that they're having to sell in the way that they're having to sell."

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes could be the next player to leave Newcastle (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

‌



While attention is returning to the club game, England fans and players will still feel some disappointment after their 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals. Tuchel has been heavily criticised for his approach during the closing stages after the Three Lions went 1-0 up through Anthony Gordon, but Heskey believes the players must also take some responsibility.

"Look, everyone's disappointed," he says. "You've got to remember there's sometimes mentality and sometimes thought process, everything just goes out the window. This is where I say we need leaders as well, because you can tell me one thing and if it's difficult, if it's different on the pitch, I've got to be able to change that myself.

"I've played in teams where we change certain things because it's just not working and you could see it wasn't working. So why not change it? Why not, on the pitch, change it? I'm a centre forward. I hold the ball up, and I run the channels. I make and create fouls.

‌



"I give ourselves a little bit of breathing space. We didn't have any of that. Everything kept on coming back in.

"It's common sense sometimes and I'm not blaming the players as such, but they've got to take some blame as well. They've got to be held accountable as well because you're on the pitch. Sometimes I might see something from the side that is totally different to when you're actually in the heat of the battle, and you need those leaders to say, 'do this, step up there,' because you just hold the ball up, just do this or just do that.

"I played with lower teams, so we've had to do that. Playing against bigger teams and you're winning 1-0, and you're thinking how are we going to hold on to this? You do that up there; we'll do this here. Make sure you win this. Make sure you do that, and you're just constantly marshalling each other around."

‌



View 4 Images England's mentality against Argentina has been questioned (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Heskey has called for perspective on Tuchel amid calls in some quarters for his sacking. He added: "I don't think he's done a bad job if I'm honest with you. I think he picked the right players.

"There might have been a case of having, maybe a Harry Maguire. If it's right at the death, there's someone who's going to put their head on the ball, I'm pretty sure he would have.

Article continues below

"But he chose who he chose. He stood by that and you've got to respect that. We got to the semifinals. Maybe a little bit of a change in mentality, and he understands the mentality of the players more and more now in those dark situations where your back's against the wall.

"I'm disappointed because you want to go to the final, but I'm not disappointed in the same way as everyone else is."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's dream Joe Gomez replacement as Liverpool boss signs £40m former player
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola's dream Joe Gomez replacement as Liverpool boss signs £40m former player

Andoni Iraola is already feeling the pressure of dealing with another Liverpool injury crisis in defence

View 3 Images James Hill of Bournemouth would be a great signing for Liverpool (Image: Getty )

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool tenure almost got off to a perfect start last week. The Reds emerged 4-2 victors against Sunderland in their pre-season friendly.

‌



Yet the win was overshadowed, and their summer preparations were hampered by an injury to Joe Gomez. The 29-year-old started the game as centre-back and captain but went off injured in just the eighth minute.

‌



Gomez travelled back to the club’s base in Chicago after the match and will undergo tests to determine the extent of the damage on what appeared to be another muscle injury.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Iraola was perfectly clear about how huge a blow it was, calling it “the worst news”. Ordinarily, an injury picked up in a friendly would have been enough cause for disappointment. But the Basque manager’s frustration was compounded by the fact he already finds his defence threadbare - despite the campaign not having got underway yet.

Skipper Virgil van Dijk missed the friendly after being given extra time off following the Netherlands’ World Cup campaign. New signing Jeremy Jacquet, who is expected to partner the Dutchman once the campaign begins, did not feature either as a precautionary measure.

‌



And £26m signing Giovanni Leoni is still rehabilitating for the foreseeable future as he works his way back from a serious ACL injury. Such a dearth of defenders meant Mor Talla Ndiaye, 18, and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, made their debuts and both performed admirably given the situation.

But neither can be expected to feature regularly yet, and being forced to play them is hardly a good sign. As such, with Liverpool’s Premier League opener at Newcastle United less than a month away, Iraola will be desperate to add a central defender before the transfer window shuts on September 1.

View 3 Images Joe Gomez's injury has left Iraola light (Image: Getty )

‌



Given first-choice right-back Conor Bradley is set to miss a huge chunk of the season with his own knee injury, the Reds would be wise to look for a central defender who can also play right-back.

While there are many defenders on the market, signing one who can step into Iraola’s system seamlessly, requires no time to adapt to the pace of the Premier League, and still represents good value for money, is a difficult task.

Enter James Hill of Bournemouth. The 24-year-old is a player Iraola already knows well and trusts from his time with the Cherries.

‌



Hill was one of his most reliable defenders last season, having made 29 appearances in the league. The Englishman was a rock at the back, making 11.16 defensive contributions per 90 and winning 65.5% of his aerial duels as well as 63.8% of his duels overall.

No central defender managed to win more aerial duels per 90 in the league than Hill (4.88). He also showcased an ability to use the ball progressively in the manner Iraola demands from his centre-backs, creating an impressive 0.56 chances per 90.

View 3 Images Iraola and Hill enjoyed success together (Image: Getty )

‌



Centre-back is undoubtedly Hill's best position and he would slot in brilliantly alongside Van Dijk or Jacquet. Crucially, he also made three appearances at right-back last term, demonstrating his versatility. He is clearly a player that would bolster Iraola’s defence once more - this time in Liverpool's colours.

But despite a breakout season, there has been virtually zero transfer noise around Hill as of yet, meaning Liverpool have work to do if they want to land his signature. Bournemouth will want to hang onto their best players this summer, with new Cherries manager Marco Rose recently labelling him a "crucial player" for the club going forward.

As such, Liverpool would need to fork out a minimum fee of £40m - no small sum considering their other likely signings - to bring him to Anfield. But that is a fee worth paying, given the repercussions of another injury crisis at Liverpool this season would be calamitous.

‌



Another hurdle Liverpool’s negotiating team would have to navigate is convincing Hill to leave the Vitality Stadium. While that would ordinarily not have been too difficult, the defender recently heaped praise on his new manager Rose and is clearly relishing the chance to play European football next season.

He may also be tentative about coming in as a back-up, given Liverpool’s other defenders will eventually return to fitness. Hill may need assurances from Iraola about his game time, especially as he plays such a key role at Bournemouth and is tipped to be a future England international if he continues in this fashion.

Nevertheless, these are issues clubs face in most transfer dealings. Liverpool's ideal defensive signing is clear to see - all that remains now is for the club to move swiftly in order to give Iraola the best chance of success this season.

Sports.title: FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup
Sports.content:
FIFA issues new defiant statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup

FIFA have insisted that “nobody is selling football” after UEFA threatens to boycott the World Cup due to Infantino's sale plans

View Image FIFA issues new statement after UEFA threatens to boycott World Cup (Image: BSR Agency, Getty Images)

FIFA have issued a new defiant statement insisting “nobody is selling football” after UEFA threatened to boycott the World Cup.

‌



Despite the criticism of its decision to launch a consultation on selling stakes in a World Cup commercial entity to private investors, FIFA is not withdrawing the plan.

‌



Although the association have asserted they are not "selling football" in their latest statement, the consultation period will go ahead.

‌



When plans to created FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) first emerged in media reports in The Times and the Financial Times on Tuesday UEFA reacted furiously.

UEFA's 55 member associations said they would boycott the World Cup and not participate in any FIFA tournament until the plan was withdrawn.

Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino's plan for World Cup explained as FIFA put on notice over boycott READ MORE :

In a statement released on Friday morning, FIFA said: “We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday.

‌



“We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation.

⁠”Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.”

The statement continued: “FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself. Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.”

‌



CONCACAF, the confederation representing 41 nations from North and Central America, along with the Caribbean, also made clear its opposition to FIFA’s plan, saying it “rejected the proposal”.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has publicly backed the plan, with an investor group led by Thrive Eternal, founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner – waiting in the wings to secure a minority stake in the new venture.

‌



However, as European teams threaten to withdraw their involvement in tournaments the promises of huge returns to national associations if FFE goes ahead are unlikely to be honoured.

European and world leagues are also opposed to the plans – fearing that commercial imperatives will drive FIFA to hold bigger and more frequent tournaments in the future, eating even further into domestic schedules.

UEFA’s opposition to the plan, in its words, is “unanimous and unequivocal”.

‌



The European football’s governing body stated: “No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."

FIFA’s statement added that “each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future”.

Liverpool news: PSG breakthrough offers major Bradley Barcola boost as club line up move

Liverpool have welcomed just two new signings this transfer window but Andoni Iraola could soon be boosted by a major arrival

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is guiding his Liverpool players through a pre-season tour of the United States (Image: Getty)

The Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool has begun and the new manager brings with him a wave of changes. But so far, only two new recruits have arrived at Anfield in Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz.

‌



After leaving Bournemouth for the Reds, Iraola's pre-season is in full swing and Liverpool followed up a win against Sunderland with a 1-0 victory over Wrexham in New York. Rio Ngumoha's strike was the difference and he notably played out on the right wing, where the iconic Mohamed Salah would usually prowl. The Egyptian King has still not been replaced.

‌



However, Liverpool's transfer window could soon enter overdrive as they pick up their pursuit of PSG's Bradley Barcola, and they've been given a huge boost. Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer updates surrounding Anfield.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bradley Barcola boost

It is understood that Liverpool have begun negotiations with PSG over Barcola, who is valued at an eye-watering £140m. Preliminary talks with the player's representatives have already been held and the signs are encouraging.

Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star READ MORE :

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

However, it is likely the French side will want a replacement before they let a player like Barcola walk. Sky Sports Germany reports that a decisive development has taken place in talks regarding Maghnes Akliouche.

‌



PSG have been courting the Monaco dynamo for some time, but a breakthrough has now been reported. All parties are currently confident that a deal will get done.

View 3 Images Liverpool have begun talks for Barcola (Image: Getty)

Akliouche has also agreed personal terms with Luis Enrique's side and so, should he arrive as predicted, this would hand the Reds a major boost as they attempt to sign Barcola.

‌



Curtis Jones update

On the departures front, Curtis Jones has long been linked with a transfer away from Liverpool and Inter Milan are the primary suitors. Negotiations are ongoing between the two clubs, though they remain apart on valuations.

But Italian outlet La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that once Inter complete the free-agent acquisition of John Stones, they will go all in for Jones.

View 3 Images Jones could soon join Inter (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Manager Cristian Chivu is supposedly desperate to wrap up a deal for the midfielder and after a meeting two nights ago, Inter's chiefs agreed that their approach will be slow but direct.

They value the player at £21m whilst the Reds want £34m, but the Italian side are more than willing to play the waiting game. Jones came off the bench in the 1-0 victory over Wrexham and was seen in animated discussion with some of his team-mates after full-time.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
