World.title: Witness D murder case nears High Court trial
World.content:
PRETORIA - The murder case of Witness D, Marius van der Merwe, is edging closer to trial.

Prosecutors say just one piece of forensic evidence remains outstanding before former Special Task Force member Matipandile Sotheni’s case can be transferred to the High Court.

Sotheni appeared briefly in the Brakpan magistrate’s court on Thursday.

Sotheni also appeared in court with a new legal representative.

“We expect that to be finalised by the next appearance so that the matter can be moved to the next phase, being, as I understand, being transferred to the High Court for the purposes of trial,” said Piet du Plessis.

Sotheni faces 16 charges, including murder and firearm-related offences.

He pleaded not guilty and was denied bail in June.

Van Der Merwe’s family says the wait for justice has been draining.

The case has now been postponed to 9 September when the State is expected to update the court on the forensic mapping of Sotheni’s cellphone.

Until then, the Van der Merwe family says they’re holding onto hope that justice will not be delayed.

World.title: FIFA vows to go ahead with private investor proposal
World.content:
PARIS - World football's governing body FIFA vowed on Friday to press ahead with an "open and democratic" consultation on a proposed private investment plan despite widespread opposition to the proposal.

That opposition included a pledge by Europe's governing body UEFA to boycott the World Cup if FIFA went ahead with its private investor plan.

FIFA said in a statement all of its member associations should have a chance to consider the plan.

"Nobody is selling football," it said.

"This is not something FIFA would ever entertain."

It also said it had heard feedback from UEFA and CONCACAF, the governing body for football in North and Central America, which said all 41 of its member associations had rejected FIFA's proposal to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup.

The world body also said its planned consultation process had been "disrupted by incorrect media reports".

"We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation," FIFA's statement said.

"We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each (member association) has the ability to express its vote based on facts," it said.

FIFA has said the plan it announced on Tuesday could raise up to $4.2 billion based on a valuation of $20 billion for the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), the commercial subsidiary it proposed to run events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

If approved, the project could provide each of FIFA's 211 member associations with a one-off payment of $20 million in early 2027 and increase their funding allocation for the 2027-2030 cycle from $8.0 million to $20 million.

Private investors would be allowed under the proposal to acquire stakes in the company but would remain minority shareholders.

- 'Never again' -

UEFA said in an earlier statement none of its national teams would participate in any FIFA competition "for so long as these proposals remain alive".

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product... No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale," it said.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino described the initiative on Wednesday as a "golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally".

However, UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, who boycotted the World Cup final to show unhappiness with FIFA, said there was no place in world football for such a model.

"Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return," he said.

"Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain."

Several leading European federations and European Union officials also criticised the proposal as another step in the commercialisation of sport, while also raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest.

The EU praised UEFA on Thursday for "defending the integrity of the game".

"Proud to see Europe's football associations leading on governance, standing firm on their principles," European commissioner for sports Glenn Micallef said in a social media post.

CONCACAF members, including the three co-hosts of the recent World Cup, unanimously rejected the proposal on Thursday.

It said "the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies".

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has also expressed concern that the FIFA proposal was made public before all 211 member associations were fully consulted.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has also urged its members to review FIFA's divisive plan.

- 'Never for sale' -

UEFA said in its statement on Thursday that the World Cup was "one of football's greatest sporting legacies" and described the proposal as "a failure of leadership" and "governance by intimidation".

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game," UEFA said.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum -- accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences.

"Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

World.title: Italy's Po River valley on drought alert
World.content:
ROME - Italian authorities raised the drought alert level to "high" on Thursday in the Po Valley, home of the country's longest river, due to worsening conditions and unfavourable weather forecasts.

More than 100 municipalities in Italy's northern regions of Piedmont and Lombardy are already facing water supply difficulties, the Po River Authority (ADBPO) said.

Some are using tanker trucks to fill drinking water reservoirs, it added.

At the foot of the Alps, Lake Maggiore and Lake Como saw their water levels drop in a week by seven percent and six percent respectively, according to the ADBPO, after water from the lake was used to help irrigate fields throughout the dried-up valley with water stored during the winter.

As in much of Europe, summer arrived too early in Italy's northern regions -- including in northwestern Veneto, which is also facing shortages.

After a dry spring, the months of June and July have seen record heat that has melted snow reserves.

Twenty river basins in Italy's north, where a new heatwave is expected to arrive on Friday, have already been granted permission to bypass minimum water flows in rivers to avoid a destructive farmland drought like that of 2022.

Around Turin and even in the centre of the Piedmontese capital, the Po has become covered with aquatic plants and algae, stimulated by the heatwave, an AFP photographer said.

In the rice fields between Turin and Milan, "the intense heat of recent days, on top of the severe water stress affecting the rice-growing area, risks compromising the entire season's production", farming union Confagricoltura said.

Despite a short spell of recent rainfall, the north has less water in lakes and rivers than it did 10 days ago, when the authority last met, said ABDPO Secretary General Alessandro Delpiano.

"Let's not fool ourselves into thinking that summer storms can solve deep-rooted problems," he added.

The heatwave that parched Europe in June would have been almost impossible without climate change, according to climatologists from the World Weather Attribution group (WWA).

World.title: Fuel price relief goes up in smoke as diesel hike looms
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Hopes for a fuel price cut have gone up in smoke.

Rising tensions between the US and Iran have reignited a rise in oil prices, wiping out the fuel over-recoveries that had motorists hoping for a sizeable cut at the pumps.

The petrol price relief has all but disappeared, while diesel users now face hefty increases in August.

Month-end data from the Central Energy Fund shows a flat 95 grade, while 93 only shows a marginal 5 cent per litre decrease.

Diesel, however, is set for increases of between R1.75 and R1.91 per litre.

The reversal follows a surge in oil prices and a weaker rand.

World.title: New North West police commissioner targets illegal mining
World.content:
MAHIKENG - The new man in charge of the North West police promises to hit the ground running, with a focus on fighting illegal mining.

Arthur Peter Adams takes over the reins from 1 August.

He says communities should not be forced to tolerate the lawlessness caused by illegal miners.

Adams brings to the North West table his 34 years of policing experience.

He acknowledges the task ahead is a mammoth one.

The challenges in the North West province run deep, and police departments are not exempt.

The provincial government has pledged full support to the new commissioner in the fight against crime.

But Premier Lazarus Mokgosi is also urging stricter police discipline amid current corruption probes.

Adams has urged police to stay focused and not let the dark cloud over the department distract them from their duties.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Madlanga Commission continues IDAC probe
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Madlanga Commission continues its focus into governance failures within Independent Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC)

An investigator from the directorate is expected to take the stand on Friday. The inquiry has so far heard allegations of misconduct by senior IDAC officials including its former head, Andrea Johnson.

Witnesses have made claims about irregular conduct and decision-making involving members of IDAC's leadership.

World.title: Mapisa-Nqakula trial witness says she received anonymous threat
World.content:
PRETORIA - A new witness in the corruption trial of Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula says she received an anonymous threat last week.

Moira Seape says the message accused her of helping IDAC investigators build what it called a non-existent case.

She is the one who introduced Mapisa-Nqakula to defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlovu.

Mapisa-Nqakula denies ever soliciting or accepting bribes from Ntsondwa-Ndlovu.

She, however, concedes that Ntsondwa-Ndlovu visited her home, but claims the visits were innocent.

The defence also rejected Ntsondwa-Ndlovu's claim that a request for a "wig" in November 2018 was a code word for money.

Seape told the court she arranged their meeting at the late Defence Secretary Sam Gulube's request, insisting nothing improper took place.

Seape also revealed she received an anonymous threat last week, accusing her of helping IDAC investigators build a "non-existent case" and warning her to be careful.

Two new witnesses are expected to take the stand on Friday.

World.title: Police brutality claims emerge in Matlala trial
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Claims of police brutality have emerged in the trial within a trial in the attempted murder case against Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala and others.

Alleged hitman Musa Kekana has claimed that law enforcement officers viciously assaulted and suffocated him during his arrest in a desperate attempt to locate firearms tied to a string of high-profile hit jobs.

Kekana is challenging the admissibility of evidence obtained during his arrest in April 2024.

According to Kekana, police tortured him in pursuit of weapons linked to the murder of Vereeniging engineer Armand Swart.

The same firearms are allegedly connected to a series of botched assassination attempts targeted at businessman Joe Sibanyoni, DJ Vettys, and Vusimuzi Matlala's former lover, Tebogo Thobejane.

State witness Captain Phimi Sekgobela rejected Kekana’s claims, maintaining that Kekana was fully cooperative. He says an ambulance was called when Kekana began coughing up blood.

Kekana also denies being the owner of the Hyundai i20 found on his property that had the firearms.

The defence included Kekana's medical record as evidence.

Cross-examination continues on Friday with Sekgobela back in the witness box.

World.title: Deputy OCS, three officers arrested over alleged kidnapping
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy OCS, three officers arrested over alleged kidnapping. [File, Standard]

A Deputy Officer Commanding Station (OCS) attached to Drive In Police Station in Nairobi North Sub-county and three other police officers have been arrested in connection with an alleged kidnapping with intent to commit a felony.

The officers are suspected of abducting a couple in Babadogo and demanding a Sh1 million ransom.

According to a police report seen by The Standard, the complainants, Kanuti Konrid and Beatrice Naliaka Njoroge, who run an online business, had travelled to Babadogo to deliver a watch to a client who had placed an order.

Upon arrival, they were allegedly confronted by three men who forced them into a waiting vehicle, where two other men were seated.

"The complainant was handcuffed and the vehicle sped off towards Thika Road. They were taken to Shell Roasters along Thika Road, where they were forced to withdraw money," the police report reads.

The report states that the complainants managed to withdraw Sh17,000, but the suspects rejected the amount and allegedly demanded Sh1 million instead.

The suspects then drove to Equity Bank in Githurai, where they allegedly ordered the complainants to withdraw the money. The wife was held hostage inside the vehicle while the husband was allowed to enter the bank.

Once inside, the husband alerted a bank teller, who informed police officers guarding the premises. The officers raised an alarm, attracting other patrol officers to the scene.

"Upon seeing the officers approaching, three suspects fled on foot while the driver sped away with the female victim. The officers fired warning shots into the air and managed to corner and arrest one suspect, Stephen Okello."

Okello was escorted to Kasarani Police Station, where he allegedly told investigators that they were five suspects using his Toyota Axio during the operation.

Police say further investigations led to the arrest of the Deputy OCS attached to Drive Inn Police Station, Kelvin Mwangi, alongside Oliver Baraza, Job Sidiga and Cyrus Onyango.

Police recovered five mobile phones valued at Sh120,000 and an Apple smartwatch valued at Sh2,500.

World.title: Ruto calls for national dialogue to shape Kenya's vision
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto has invited Kenyans to take part in what he described as the country's most significant national conversation since the adoption of the 2010 Constitution, saying the discussions will help chart Kenya's next long-term development agenda.

Speaking on the country's development trajectory, the President said the conversation should move beyond partisan politics and election cycles to focus on a shared national vision.

"I invite every Kenyan to what I believe will become the most consequential national conversation since the adoption of our Constitution in 2010," Ruto said.

"A national conversation about Kenya's development. This conversation must rise above politics, transcend electoral cycles and unite us around a shared destiny."

The President acknowledged that while Vision 2030 had set an ambitious goal of transforming Kenya into an upper-middle-income country by 2030, the country remains off course to achieve that target.

"Vision 2030 set a target of Kenya becoming an upper-middle-income country by 2030. So far, we are off target. This is not a criticism of Vision 2030, nor is it a reason for disappointment; rather, it is an opportunity to learn from our successes proudly, reflect with honesty on where we have fallen short, and define together Kenya's next long-term vision," he said.

At the same time, Ruto announced that the government will formally launch a nationwide conversation on August 12 to develop Kenya's next long-term development blueprint as Vision 2030 nears its end.

"Accordingly, on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, we shall formally launch the National Conversation on Kenya's Future Beyond Vision 2030; the most consequential exercise in national reflection and public participation since the promulgation of our Constitution in 2010," he stated.

Ruto said recent economic reforms had laid a stronger foundation for future growth, citing improvements in key macroeconomic indicators.

"We have stabilized our currency, inflation has fallen, borrowing costs have declined, and investor confidence has returned," he said. "Last year Kenya attracted a record $3.2 billion in foreign direct investment, more than double the amount recorded in 2022."

He added that Kenya's improving investment climate had earned international recognition.

"The 2025 IMD World Competitiveness Ranking placed Kenya as the most competitive economy in Africa, reflecting the confidence our reforms have restored," Ruto said.

At the same time, Ruto also highlighted the establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund and the Sovereign Wealth Fund, saying the two institutions would help finance strategic investments while safeguarding the country's wealth for future generations.

According to Ruto, Kenya must now confront difficult questions about its development path to unlock its full potential.

"The question we must ask ourselves candidly and honestly is why other nations have fulfilled so much of their potential while we have repeatedly fallen short. What must we now do differently to ensure that the next chapter of Kenya's development story is fundamentally different from the last?" he posed.

He urged all Kenyans to help shape a new long-term national vision, saying the country's future depends on collective commitment rather than political divisions.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Egyptian fencing team defeats Israel to claim World Championship team bronze
World.content:
The Egyptian national sabre fencing team secured the bronze medal after defeating Israel with a score of 39–38 at the World Fencing Championships (Team Epee/Sabre) held in Hong Kong, marking a historic achievement.

The Pharaohs edged out their opponent 39–38 during the Senior World Championships hosted by Hong Kong from July 22 to 30.

The national team kicked off its campaign with a 44–33 victory over Portugal in the Round of 32, followed by a tight 36–35 win against Spain in the Round of 16.

Egypt then advanced to the semifinals after defeating Russia 45–35.

Although the team suffered a 41–32 loss to Kazakhstan in the semifinal round, they rallied to clinch the bronze medal by overcoming Israel 39–38 in the third-place match.

The Egyptian delegation is led by the President of the Egyptian Fencing Federation, Captain Tarek al-Hossainy, and the Director of National Fencing Teams, Ayman Ghoneim, who serves as administrative manager.

The medical staff includes Dr. Magdy al-Sabbagh as team physician, along with physical therapists Ahmed Abdel-Ghani and Ghada Atef.

Also accompanying the delegation is the Vice President of the Egyptian Fencing Federation, Ahmed Samir, upon an invitation from the International Fencing Federation (FIE) to attend the FIE Referees Commission meetings—in his capacity as Chairman of the African Fencing Confederation’s Supreme Referees Committee—as well as the IOC Safe Sport meetings held on the sidelines of the World Championship.

World.title: Amr Adib calls for ‘firm response’ to Damietta Port drone attack
World.content:
Egyptian TV host Amr Adib commented on the fire that broke out on two ships at Damietta Port following a drone strike, stressing that Egypt’s response to this breach must be firm and direct, RT Arabic reported.

In a post shared on his official X (formerly Twitter) account, Adib highlighted that the current situation demands a strict stance, writing: “Egypt’s must be strong, forceful, and clear. Those advocating for self-restraint should remain completely silent.”

He added: “Knowing the source of the drone is not impossible. A strike must be met with a harsher strike so we do not receive more drones. This is a case of self-defense, and no one can stop you or blame you under any law. Anyone who harbors ill intentions toward Egypt must pay a heavy price.”

Adib’s remarks follow an official statement issued by the Egyptian Cabinet, which confirmed that the fire aboard the two vessels at Damietta Port resulted from a drone strike, adding that no entity has claimed responsibility for the incident so far.

World.title: IMF to provide $1.774 billion to Egypt following final Executive Board approval
World.content:
The Executive Director at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) representing the Arab Group and Maldives on the Executive Board, Mohamed Maait, anticipates the transfer of the seventh tranche under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) program with Egypt, alongside the second tranche under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF)—totaling $1.774 billion—within five business days following final board approval and the endorsement of the seventh review scheduled for Thursday, in Washington, D.C.

The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) is expected to receive the disbursed funds early next week, following the inclusion of Egypt’s dossier on the agenda of the Executive Board meeting to consider the approval of the seventh review under the EFF arrangement.

Maait explained that Egypt will receive a total payout of $1.774 billion within days.

This includes $1.5 billion for the seventh review of the core EFF arrangement and approximately $274 million designated under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility to finance environmental and climate projects in Egypt.

He emphasized that the final value of both tranches remains subject to precise calculations tied to exchange rates and Special Drawing Rights.

IMF-supported financing program

This comes within the framework of an IMF-supported financing program for Egypt, which encompasses an eight billion dollar Extended Fund Facility alongside an additional $1.3 billion provided through the Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

The former Chairman of the Plan and Budget Committee in the House of Representatives and Professor of Economics at Cairo University, Fakhri al-Feky, expects that the two IMF tranches will help boost foreign exchange reserves at the Central Bank, foster greater local exchange rate stability, and cover certain international financial obligations related to foreign debt installments.

However, Professor of Economics at Cairo University Medhat Nafei, called for reducing or waiving a portion of the interest due on external debt, particularly as the government paid over eight billion dollars in interest during 2025 alone.

He clarified that these mentioned obligations do not represent debt principal installments, but rather interest payments, highlighting the pressing need to invest in human resources instead of debt service.

“In 2025, external debt service payments reached $33.4 billion, comprising $25.36 billion in principal repayments and $8.06 billion in interest—meaning that roughly 24 percent of total payments went strictly toward interest,” Nafei stated.

He added that debt service payments decreased in 2025 by approximately 13.6% compared to 2024, describing this as a positive development.

He noted that the true challenge lies not only in reducing total payments but also in curbing reliance on high-cost borrowing so that state resources can shift from interest servicing to funding economic development.

World.title: Nearly 2,900 dead as early heatwaves strike the UK
World.content:
British authorities announced that 2,887 people died during the two heatwaves that struck the country in May and June.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stated in a Thursday press release that the estimated figure of 2,887 heat-related deaths in May and June highlights the significant impact of these two heatwaves on public health, particularly as the casualties occurred early in the summer season.

The agency noted that this figure is nearly double the total heat-related deaths recorded during the entire summer of 2025.

British authorities declared a drought across nearly half of England on Wednesday, following a sharp decline in rainfall during July, coinciding with record-breaking heatwaves reaching 38°C (100.4°F) and a severe depletion of rivers and reservoirs.

World.title: Traffic Authority announces major Cairo road closures and North Coast speed limit upgrades
World.content:
Traffic expert Ahmed Hisham confirmed that the General Directorate of Traffic, in coordination with the traffic departments across the Greater Cairo governorates, is readying to handle the heavy travel flow usually seen at the end of the workweek.

During a phone interview with Nihad Samir on the “Sada al-Balad” channel, Hisham explained that the General Directorate of Traffic has intensified its services on highways using motorcycle units, rapid response recovery vehicles, four-wheel-drive vehicles, fixed and mobile checkpoints, alongside speed radars.

He noted the ongoing traffic closure on Haram Street in Giza Governorate to accommodate the construction of seven stations for Phase II of the Cairo Metro Line IV.

He advised drivers to use the Tersa Street and King Faisal Street as alternative routes to ease congestion, especially for those arriving from the Cairo–Alexandria Desert Road and the Cairo–Fayoum Desert Road.

Hisham added that there is a total closure on North 90th Street due to repairs for a road subsidence, with traffic diversions in place for vehicles heading toward Suez Road for 48 hours.

Furthermore, Ibn Sandar Street is closed for 72 hours from its intersection with Saray El Qobba Street to Ibn Aqil Street, with traffic diversions implemented to smooth the flow.

He concluded by announcing the completion of development work on the 135-kilometer Wadi El Natrun–El Alamein Road, which connects the Cairo–Alexandria Desert Road with the North Coast.

The road is operating at full capacity with five lanes in each direction, and the General Directorate of Traffic has raised the official speed limit on it from 100 to 120 km/h.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egypt assures Damietta Port operating at ‘full capacity’ following drone attack
World.content:
The Ministry of Transport announced that Damietta Port is operating at its full operational capacity, following a drone strike that caused a fire at the port.

All operational activities at the port are proceeding normally and regularly, with the continuous arrival and departure of various types of vessels, alongside ongoing cargo handling, stevedoring, container operations, dry bulk, liquid bulk, and general cargo operations.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the ministry stated that all berths and terminals at the port are operating with full efficiency, supported by the complete availability of maritime and logistical services, including pilotage, towing, and mooring.

This ensures swift vessel turnaround times and minimizes port stay duration, in line with the Ministry of Transport’s plan to enhance the efficiency of Egyptian ports and raise their regional and international competitiveness.

The ministry added that Damietta Port continues to offer its services 24/7 through an integrated operational framework powered by the latest technologies.

This contributes to meeting the requirements of global shipping lines and port users, ensuring a smooth flow of trade and supply chains without obstacles.

The ministry affirmed that handling operations across all sectors remain consistent, with cargo loading, unloading, storage, and internal transport adhering to the highest safety and efficiency standards to meet performance targets and maintain uninterrupted export and import flows.

A vital port

The ministry highlighted that Damietta Port is one of Egypt’s most vital commercial ports and a major hub within the maritime transport and logistics network.

It receives significant attention under the state’s strategy to develop Egyptian ports and transform Egypt into a regional hub for transport, logistics, and transit trade—achieved through berth and terminal expansion projects, infrastructure upgrades, and the modernization of operational systems and services.

The Ministry of Transport concluded its statement by emphasizing its round-the-clock monitoring of all operational activities at Damietta Port.

This ensures the continuous delivery of high-quality services, maintains the steady flow of maritime navigation and cargo handling, and supports trade movement—thereby bolstering the status of Egyptian ports and advancing the nation’s economic development goals.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Explosions reported in southern Iran after US launches new strikes. Here’s the latest
World.content:
Explosions were heard tonight in several locations in southern Iran as the US military launched more strikes against the country.

The attacks come following a warning from President Donald Trump, who vowed to forcefully respond to Iran’s attempted missile attack a day earlier on US forces in the Middle East.

“We’re going to be hitting them very hard because it’s our turn to hit them. They know it’s coming,” he told reporters in the Oval Office.

Here’s what else you should know:

World.title: Poland blames Russia for firing missile into its territory as Moscow unleashes deadly attack on Ukraine
World.content:
Kyiv, Ukraine —

A missile apparently fired by Russia landed deep inside Polish territory, Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Thursday, as Moscow launched deadly long-range attacks across Ukraine that killed at least eight people.

The missile landed and exploded about 90 kilometers (55 miles) into Polish territory early Thursday, leaving a massive crater in the middle of a field, local authorities said.

“We were prepared to shoot down the missile if it had continued its flight,” Tusk told an emergency government meeting, according to his office on X. “All indications suggest that it was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile.”

Two NATO fighter jets, a NATO refueling aircraft, a Polish early warning aircraft and a Polish helicopter were deployed to counter the threat, a spokesperson for the alliance told CNN.

NATO will “continue to take all necessary measures to defend NATO territory, General Alexus G. Grynkewich, the alliance’s Supreme Allied Commander for Europe, said in a statement to CNN.

Still, there are no reasons to think Poland was the intended target, Tusk said later when he visited the crater site, according to Reuters.

Poland had earlier reported scrambling fighter jets in response to a major Russian attack on Ukraine, which hit large swathes of the country, killed at least eight people, including children, and left dozens more injured or trapped under rubble.

Any potential Russian attack so deep inside a NATO member’s territory would risk being perceived as an escalation in Moscow’s yearslong war on Ukraine. It is not the first time Poland has reported a “Russian-made” missile landing inside its territory – but this one reached unusually far. In November 2022, one struck and killed two people but that incident was only 4 miles (6.4 kilometers) from the Ukrainian border.

The attacks come days after Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to the United States to again plead for more air defenses, as Russia fires more ballistic missiles into Ukraine and intensifies its air assaults on the country’s cities. As a result, more Ukrainian civilians have been killed this month than in any since April 2022. At the same time, Kyiv is emphasizing its ability to hit deep inside Russia, attacking Wildberries facilities, often described as “Russia’s Amazon,” across the border.

People take shelter inside a metro station during a Russian missile and drone strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Thursday, July 30. Alina Smutko/Reuters

Deadly strikes in Ukraine

This wave of attacks killed at least eight people across the country, according to its foreign minister Andrii Sybiha, including six members of a single family.

In the village of Radushne, near Zelensky’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih, parents and four children were killed after a ballistic missile blew a family home “into smithereens,” Zelensky said. Two more children were pulled alive from the rubble, he added.

Two girls, aged 5 and 12, were among the four children killed, Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the southern Ukrainian city’s military administration, said on Telegram, calling it a “dark night.”

Graphic video from Radushne showed bodies strewn amid the rubble of a shattered building, with fires still burning.

Two unseen women could be heard speaking. “We’ve pulled one child out. There are still some lying over there,” one said.

“There are children here. There are many children,” the other said.

In Lviv, emergency workers rescued an injured 10-year-old boy, who was carried away on a stretcher, as they raced to save people trapped under rubble after an attack on a residential building. Dozens across the country were wounded.

Missile crater in Poland

The missile crashed in an undeveloped area near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia in Lublin province, Poland’s army said. Polish police said residents reported hearing a powerful blast.

Separately, Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said a Russian cruise missile had “crossed into Poland as part of Russia’s massive strike against Ukraine” in a post to X.

Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it carried out a “massive strike using long-range precision weapons from land, air, and sea” as well as attack drones on military sites across Ukraine, in a statement posted to Telegram Thursday.

Poland’s army said the country’s air defenses observed at least a dozen missiles over western Ukraine, which posed a potential threat to Polish airspace.

The attack damaged or destroyed dozens of homes, businesses and infrastructure facilities, Zelensky said on Telegram Thursday, and used more than 70 missiles and over 280 attack drones.

Ukraine intercepted more than 260 drones, according to Zelensky, in what he said was a commendable feat given a “critical shortage of air defense missiles from our partners.”

On his way home on Wednesday, Zelensky stopped in the Polish city of Lublin – not far from the site of the next day’s crash – to meet with Tusk. The two leaders discussed “the outcomes of (Zelensky’s) visit to the United States and the security of Poland, Ukraine, and all of Europe,” according to a post to X by Tusk.

Poland has routinely scrambled jets in response to Russian attacks on western Ukraine, though they have rarely entered its territory. NATO fighter jets shot down multiple Russian drones that violated Polish airspace last September, denouncing Moscow for “absolutely dangerous behavior.”

This story has been updated with additional developments.

World.title: Zambia’s Ambassador  to China Zyuulu has died

Mr Kangwa said that the funeral gathering is at House No. 28, Boniface Simutowe Road, Presidential Housing Initiative (PHI), Lusaka.

World.title: UPND accuses Mundubile of politicising Solwezi musicians incident
World.content:
UPND accuses Mundubile of politicising Solwezi incident before police conclude investigations

The United Party for National Development (UPND) has accused National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) presidential candidate Brian Mundubile of attempting to politicise an alleged altercation involving musicians in Solwezi before police have concluded their investigations.

UPND Media Director Mark Simuuwe said Mr Mundubile’s public statements amounted to prejudging the matter and risked undermining the constitutional mandate of the Zambia Police Service to investigate criminal allegations independently and without political interference.

The remarks follow Mr Mundubile’s claims linking President Hakainde Hichilema and the ruling UPND to the reported incident in Solwezi, allegations the governing party has dismissed as unfounded and politically motivated.

In a statement issued in Lusaka, Mr Simuuwe said the opposition leader was seeking to exploit an incident that remains under active police investigation.

“Facing the overwhelming momentum of President Hakainde Hichilema’s nationwide campaign, a panicked opposition has realised that defeat is imminent and is resorting to manufacturing lies and desperate tactics. Zambia is a nation of laws. Let the police execute their constitutional mandate without political interference or pressure,” Mr Simuuwe said.

He maintained that the UPND government had dismantled political cadreism and violence in public spaces and did not shield individuals suspected of committing criminal offences, regardless of political affiliation.

Mr Simuuwe urged the Zambia Police Service in North-Western Province to carry out a thorough, professional and impartial investigation to establish the facts surrounding the reported altercation.

He also challenged Mr Mundubile to hand over any evidence in his possession to investigators instead of litigating the matter through public statements.

“Mr Mundubile asserts that his party possesses video footage identifying the alleged perpetrators. If he is sincere about seeking justice rather than orchestrating a political stunt, we challenge him to immediately submit this unedited footage directly to the police,” he said.

Mr Simuuwe said pursuing the matter through social media before investigations were complete risked undermining due process and inflaming political tensions at a time when the country was preparing for the August 13 general election.

He further defended the constitutional rights of artists, musicians and performers to freely associate with any political party or movement without intimidation, harassment or violence.

According to the UPND, attempts to implicate President Hichilema in isolated incidents ignored the Head of State’s repeated calls for peaceful campaigns and his consistent instructions to party members and security agencies to uphold law, order and democratic discipline throughout the election period.

Mr Simuuwe said assigning blame before police establish the facts served neither justice nor the public interest, adding that political leaders should allow law enforcement agencies to discharge their constitutional responsibilities independently.

He urged all political parties to focus on issue-based campaigns rather than exploit unverified incidents for political gain, saying Zambians expected leaders to present practical solutions to the country’s challenges instead of heightening political tensions through speculation.

“UPND remains committed to a peaceful, issue-based campaign and calls on all stakeholders to safeguard the peace and unity that Zambia is known for,” Mr Simuuwe said.

He added that since assuming office, President Hichilema’s administration had taken deliberate steps to eliminate political violence and restore law and order, reaffirming the government’s commitment to peaceful democratic engagement.

Police have already opened investigations into the reported Solwezi incident, with authorities expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged altercation before determining whether any criminal offences were committed.

World.title: Samukonga qualifies for 400m final
World.content:
Sprinter Muzala Samukonga has qualified for the men’s 400m final at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Samukonga put himself in the right position to defend the title he won at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games after a semifinal triumph.

He finished second in his semi-final after clocking 45.95s.

UK’s Thomas Reynolds won the race after clocking 45.63s.

Samukonga’s compatriots Patrick Nyambe and Kennedy Luchembe also recorded impressive results in their respective men’s 400m semi-finals. Nyambe clocked 46.50s while Luchembe clocked 46.60s.

In the women’s 400m semi-final, Niddy Mingilishi clocked 55.10s.

Despite their determined performances, Nyambe, Luchembe, and Mingilishi did not progress to the men’s and women’s 400m finals.

The trio will now shift focus to the 4x400m mixed relay, where they will join the rest of Team Zambia’s relay squad in pursuit of a strong performance.

Samukonga remains Zambia’s sole representative in the men’s 400m final as he bids for a medal.

Meanwhile, the National Olympic Committee of Zambia – NOCZ has applauded the performance of boxer Albert Ngulube despite his elimination from the Commonwealth Games.

Ngulube was eliminated from the Men’s 60kg category at the quarter-final stage.

“The young Zambian boxer earned widespread admiration for the spirited performance he delivered against defending Commonwealth champion Jude Gallagher of Northern Ireland. Ngulube pushed the experienced champion all the way in a closely contested contest that was decided by a 2–3 split decision, highlighting the determination, skill and composure he displayed on one of boxing’s biggest stages,” NOCZ stated.

“Making his Commonwealth Games debut, Ngulube proved he belongs among the elite, giving Team Zambia and the nation plenty to be proud of. His courageous display has marked him as one of Zambia’s exciting boxing prospects,” NOCZ added.

World.title: Mundubile promises ministry of chiefs revival, mineral royalties for traditional leaders
World.content:
Mundubile pledges to restore ministry of chiefs, as Milupi accuses him of dishonest campaigning

National Restoration and Progressive Union Party presidential candidate Brian Mundubile says he will restore the ministry of chiefs and traditional affairs to address the declining recognition of traditional leaders in the political space.

Speaking during a courtesy call on acting Chief Musele at Kasisa Palace, Mr Mundubile said his government, if elected, would ensure traditional leaders are paid royalties from minerals extracted in their chiefdoms.

“When we go to an area, before we do any activities, we make sure that we pay homage to the traditional leaders. We do that because we have seen some declining recognition of our traditions and indeed, especially in the political space, so we want to make sure that we keep the tradition because that’s who we are,” he said.

Mr Mundubile said mining companies should improve the welfare of miners. He said royalty is paid to chiefdoms where these resources are extracted, and traditional leaders together with citizens, through a trust, will begin to develop their areas.

He said mining companies should also provide proper accommodation for mine workers and improve local infrastructure in areas where mining takes place.

“This copper they are mining here is the same copper Zambia used to mine under ZCCM, that’s what built Chingola. You’ve seen how Chingola looks, isn’t it? Can you compare it with Kisasa? Can you compare Chililabombwe with Kisasa? Can you compare Ndola with Kisasa? Can you compare Kitwe with Kisasa? It’s the same copper that we used to mine on our own,” he said.

Mr Mundubile urged President Hakainde Hichilema to publicly denounce violence being perpetrated by alleged UPND cadres. He added that the President should direct police to bring the culprits to book.

Meanwhile, UPND Alliance chairperson Charles Milupi has accused Mr Mundubile of running a dishonest campaign in North Western Province. Mr Milupi said the NRPUP leader and his running mate Makebi Zulu have been misleading Zambians during rallies in the region.

Speaking during his own engagement in the province, Mr Milupi said Mr Mundubile’s characterisation of North Western Province as developmentally neglected does not reflect the historical record.

He cited the Mutanda-Mwinilunga road and other infrastructure projects delivered under the New Dawn administration as evidence contradicting Mr Mundubile’s claims.

“Those PF guys are people we buried at the graveyard when they lost in 2021, and should not be brought back through the Tonse Alliance,” President Hichilema separately said at a rally in Western Province, reinforcing the ruling party’s message that opposition figures represent a return to past governance failures.

President Hichilema said PF was rejected in 2021 and should not be brought back through the Tonse Alliance. He said some independents were secretly being supported by figures within the ruling party’s own base, warning against being cheated by such claims.

The exchange between the two campaigns comes as the countdown to the August 13 general election intensifies, with both sides sharpening their messaging on traditional leadership, development records and campaign conduct in the closing stretch of the race.

World.title: All ballot papers now in Zambia ahead of August 13 polls
World.content:
ECZ completes ballot delivery as final consignment arrives in Lusaka

The Electoral Commission of Zambia has received the final consignment of ballot papers for the August 13 general election. This completes a key stage of election preparations.

The last shipment, comprising 185 pallets of ballot papers, arrived at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport. It came aboard an ER-BAS Boeing 747 chartered aircraft from Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

ECZ chief electoral officer Brown Kasaro received the consignment. He was joined by political party representatives, civil society organisations and other election stakeholders.

The delivery brings the total to 387 ballot paper pallets. This follows Wednesday’s consignment of 202 pallets.

“In today’s consignment, we have the last 185 pallets of ballot papers. Together with yesterday’s consignment of 202 pallets, this marks the completion of the delivery, a total of 387 ballot paper pallets and related election documents,” Mr Kasaro said.

He described the arrival of the final consignment as another major milestone in the commission’s preparations. He said the printing and delivery of all ballot papers has now been successfully completed.

Mr Kasaro said stakeholders accompanied the ballot papers from the airport to the ECZ warehouse in Silverest, Chongwe District. Verification of the ballots will begin there before similar inspections are conducted in all districts.

He said verification at a national level would not be the final stage. Similar exercises would be conducted in all districts before dispatch to polling stations.

“Verification here at head office is not the final stage, as this will be conducted in each constituency in the presence of stakeholders before final dispatch to polling stations in readiness for poll day,” he said.

The completion of the ballot delivery process attracted commendation from political parties and election observers. They said ECZ maintained openness throughout the printing, transportation and receipt of the ballots.

UPND media director Mark Simuuwe said the involvement of stakeholders at every stage has enhanced confidence in the electoral process. He expressed hope that the commission will maintain the same level of transparency until polling day.

He also dismissed allegations that opposition political leaders had been barred from using Zambia’s airspace. He said NRPUP president Brian Mundubile’s remarks that his party was voluntarily travelling by road had disproved the claims.

Pamodzi Alliance secretary general Celestine Mukandila said ECZ has upheld democratic principles by ensuring all critical electoral processes are conducted in full view of stakeholders.

Citizens First Lusaka Province secretary Glenda Tupa also welcomed the commission’s openness. She said the process has inspired confidence among participating stakeholders.

Southern African Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Disputes executive director Arthur Muyunda urged political players and members of the public to avoid spreading misinformation. He said such misinformation was capable of undermining public confidence in the elections.

Civic Society Alliance on Legal Reforms vice-chairperson David Mbula said the transparent handling of the ballot papers reflected the commission’s commitment to accountability. This spanned from arrival at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport to the ECZ warehouse.

Non-governmental Gender Organisations’ Coordinating Council board chairperson Beauty Katebe said the transparent process has strengthened the credibility of the forthcoming general election.

World.title: NGOCC presses police over perceived bias in election violence cases
World.content:
NGOCC urges police impartiality as concerns mount over election violence

The Non-Governmental Gender Organisations Coordinating Council has called on the Zambia Police Service to reflect on public perception that it is handling election-related violence with bias.

NGOCC board publicity secretary Liya Mitaba raised the concern at a press briefing. She said the council remained equally troubled by persistently low representation of women among validly nominated candidates ahead of next month’s general elections.

“It is just a reminder to the police that if the public is perceiving them as being unfair, can they please reflect? If it’s true, can they address that issue because it also undermines public integrity and trust in these institutions,” she said.

Ms Mitaba said her organisation has consistently called on all government agencies to exercise their duties independently. She said this applied without bias throughout the campaign period.

NGOCC said it was equally concerned by reports of violence, intimidation and political coercion. These practices, the organisation said, characterised aspects of the adoption and nomination processes within some political parties.

“Violence and manipulation have no place in a democratic society and must never become acceptable features of Zambia’s electoral process,” she said.

Ms Mitaba said such practices undermined democratic values. She said they also discouraged capable women from offering themselves for public office and weakened public confidence in internal party democracy.

Meanwhile, the organisation said nomination figures announced by the Electoral Commission of Zambia demonstrate a worrying trend. Despite constitutional reforms and repeated pledges by political parties, women continue to face significant barriers to elective leadership.

She said the statistics painted a worrying picture. Zambia remained far from achieving the 50:50 gender representation envisaged in the Constitution, the SADC Protocol on Gender and Development, the African Union Agenda 2063 and the Sustainable Development Goals.

All of these instruments recognise women’s equal participation in decision-making as fundamental to inclusive and sustainable development.

Ms Mitaba said NGOCC acknowledged political parties that had fielded female candidates. She also praised women who had stood as independent candidates despite the obstacles.

“Their determination reflects resilience in the face of considerable obstacles and serves as an inspiration to many women and girls across the country,” she said.
